a17.speaker: George Phiri, political analyst
a17.name: George Phiri
a17.title: political analyst
a17.speech: Cast doubt on the nation's independence, arguing that continued economic dependence, food insecurity, and social instability suggest Malawi has yet to attain true sovereignty. "We celebrate independence every year, but can we really claim to be independent when we cannot feed ourselves or stand without foreign aid?" ; "Our challenges in health, education, and food security are symptoms of a nation still tethered to external support." Criticized the government's dependence on donor funding, referencing the U.S. government's recent suspension of USAID support: "Independent people don't hack each other with machetes," ; "When USAID pulled out, the country came to a standstill. That's not the mark of independence—it's the sign of a fragile, dependent state."

a17.speaker: Chimwemwe Tsitsi, political analyst
a17.name: Chimwemwe Tsitsi
a17.title: political analyst
a17.speech: Acknowledges the country's struggles but maintains that achieving independence was essential: "Under colonial rule, Malawians suffered—through forced labor systems like Thangata and racial segregation. Gaining control of our destiny was a necessary step, regardless of the challenges we now face,"

a17.speaker: Chimwemwe Tsitsi, political analyst
a17.name: Chimwemwe Tsitsi
a17.title: political analyst
a17.speech: Urged a renewed focus on economic reform, particularly in empowering local ownership and rooting out corruption: "We need policies that prioritize Malawian businesses and limit foreign dominance," ; "True independence isn't just a historical event—it's a continuous effort to build a self-sustaining nation."

a112.speaker: Speakers at the decoration ceremony (Beninese officials, unnamed)
a112.name: Speakers at the decoration ceremony (Beninese officials
a112.title: unnamed)
a112.speech: The various speeches all went in the same direction, saying the distinctions came to "attest to the satisfaction of the Beninese people with regard to the work" carried out by Lee Roussel and Gloria Peterson, and praising "the calm and rigour they displayed when it came to recalling the need to respect the agreed management rules."

a112.speaker: Lee Roussel, resident director of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) in Benin, spokesperson for the two recipients
a112.name: Lee Roussel
a112.title: resident director of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) in Benin, spokesperson for the two recipients
a112.speech: At the podium, was lost for words to express their joy; moved, she dissolved into nothing but thanks.

a129.speaker: Wim Vanhelleputte, CEO of Safaricom Ethiopia
a129.name: Wim Vanhelleputte
a129.title: CEO of Safaricom Ethiopia
a129.speech: “We are excited for the opportunity to partner for a such a transformative cause, Youth Development, by availing our Fast-Data Connectivity in the youth centres and incubation hubs building the next generation talent base to meet the demands of Digital Ethiopia.”

a193.speaker: Dr. Kalumbi Shangula, Minister of Health and Social Services (Namibia)
a193.name: Dr. Kalumbi Shangula
a193.title: Minister of Health and Social Services (Namibia)
a193.speech: Has underscored the importance of public-private partnerships in achieving the Ministry's mission of providing integrated, affordable, and responsive healthcare to all Namibians.

a193.speaker: Zambezi Region health directorate
a193.name: Zambezi Region health directorate
a193.speech: According to the region's health directorate, the Zambezi Region has recorded a worrying increase in malaria cases, with 3,385 cases reported since January and one fatality in August last year.

a193.speaker: Ministry of Health and Social Services (MoHSS)
a193.name: Ministry of Health and Social Services (MoHSS)
a193.speech: Says the integration of mental health and psychological support within HIV services is key to promoting holistic care, as it will address both mental and physical health as well as improve HIV treatment adherence.

a193.speaker: Ministry of Health and Social Services (MoHSS)
a193.name: Ministry of Health and Social Services (MoHSS)
a193.speech: Has commended the contractor for the Ombili clinic in Otjiwarongo, which was completed two months ahead of time.

a193.speaker: Ministry of Health and Social Services (MoHSS)
a193.name: Ministry of Health and Social Services (MoHSS)
a193.speech: Has dismissed rumours circulating false information about the detection of monkeypox (Mpox) disease in Namibia in a social media post.

a193.speaker: Dr. Kalumbi Shangula, Minister of Health and Social Services (Namibia)
a193.name: Dr. Kalumbi Shangula
a193.title: Minister of Health and Social Services (Namibia)
a193.speech: At the opening ceremony of the African Health Workforce Investment Forum on Monday, noted that by the end of 2023, 98.5% of babies born to HIV-positive mothers in Namibia were HIV-free.

a253.speaker: Trevor Manuel, chair of the G20 panel of experts on Africa and former South African finance minister
a253.name: Trevor Manuel
a253.title: chair of the G20 panel of experts on Africa and former South African finance minister
a253.speech: Said critically needed economic growth in Africa is being held back by high borrowing costs imposed by international lenders, with unpredictable US policy changes adding to the strain ; told AFP that African nations are not necessarily more indebted than major economies but they face higher debt servicing costs ; said the “unbelievably expensive and prohibitive” cost of capital for African nations has hobbled their development ; “We know that the risk premiums in general on Africa are much higher than they need to be, and that impacts them on the debt service costs” ; said the panel will seek to persuade the entire G20 to engage with multilateral development banks, in particular the World Bank and International Monetary Fund, to address the issue of borrowing costs.

a253.speaker: Trevor Manuel, chair of the G20 panel of experts on Africa
a253.name: Trevor Manuel
a253.title: chair of the G20 panel of experts on Africa
a253.speech: Said abrupt changes in global order since US President Donald Trump took office in January, such as sweeping aid cuts and trade tariffs, will have long-lasting ramifications for the continent ; said Trump’s “capricious” announcement in April of major trade tariffs effectively did away with the African Growth and Opportunity Act, citing Lesotho, which faces 50 percent tariffs on exports to the United States, and Madagascar, threatened with 47 percent tariffs ; “It becomes unbelievably difficult for small countries that try and develop export markets, for their products to be struck by these sudden announcements. There’s no time for adjustment” ; said the termination of USAID programmes and a push for NATO countries to increase defence spending add to the pressure: “The impact on the African continent is going to be very severe. We can’t abstract Africa from the rest of the globe” ; “The realm of policymaking requires a greater degree of predictability and certainty than what we see at the moment” ; “The fact that there are these occasional outbursts that aren’t informed by reality as I see it… makes it even more complex.”

a253.speaker: Trevor Manuel, chair of the G20 panel of experts on Africa
a253.name: Trevor Manuel
a253.title: chair of the G20 panel of experts on Africa
a253.speech: Said his panel’s work on better understanding the African economy and developing solutions was likely to continue beyond this year’s G20, for example via the UN Economic Commission for Africa and the African Union, including looking at “intra-African dynamics” such as the role of the African Continental Free Trade Area ; said conflicts also cost the continent, citing the war in Sudan and unrest that has held back a major gas project in northern Mozambique: “When countries spend more on war than what they do on the upliftment of people, then we face profound consequences” ; said a strong United Nations and African Union were important in “persuading countries to do the right things” in the long term: “If you don’t have those kinds of objectives, which frequently will not be completed within a particular electoral cycle, I think we run ourselves into the ground.”

a253.speaker: South African government
a253.name: South African government
a253.speech: Says more than half of Africa’s 1.3 billion people live in countries with debt interest payments higher than social spending on health, education and infrastructure, and that African countries will pay close to $89 billion in external debt service alone this year, with 20 low-income countries at risk of debt distress.

a350.speaker: Kadidiata Diarra Badji, Director of Examinations and Competitions (DECO), Cote d'Ivoire
a350.name: Kadidiata Diarra Badji
a350.title: Director of Examinations and Competitions (DECO), Cote d'Ivoire
a350.speech: Announced on Tuesday 17 June 2025 in Abidjan the results of the 2025 session of the Brevet d'etudes du premier cycle (BEPC): in total 312,041 candidates were declared successful, a national pass rate of 51.41%, against 40.18% in 2024, an increase of 11.23 points.

a350.speaker: Kadidiata Diarra Badji, Director of Examinations and Competitions (DECO), Cote d'Ivoire
a350.name: Kadidiata Diarra Badji
a350.title: Director of Examinations and Competitions (DECO), Cote d'Ivoire
a350.speech: "The progressive improvement of pass rates is a promising indication of the revival of our education system towards greater performance and competitiveness. At the same time it is a source of satisfaction in view of the massive investments made by the State of Cote d'Ivoire," she said with satisfaction ; according to her, these convincing results of the 2025 BEPC, already perceptible at the CEPE session, are the fruit of the vision of the Minister of National Education, of her quest for a quality school and of the reforms stemming from the General Assembly on National Education and Literacy (EGENA).

a350.speaker: Kadidiata Diarra Badji, Director of Examinations and Competitions (DECO), Cote d'Ivoire
a350.name: Kadidiata Diarra Badji
a350.title: Director of Examinations and Competitions (DECO), Cote d'Ivoire
a350.speech: Also welcomed the awareness shown by candidates and the remobilisation of all the actors of the educational community around the values of work, merit and transparency: "I congratulate all those who passed. They can be proud of the work accomplished during the 2024-2025 school year, today crowned by these results. I associate with these congratulations the supervisors and the parents of pupils, true architects of this success," she declared.

a350.speaker: Kadidiata Diarra Badji, Director of Examinations and Competitions (DECO), Cote d'Ivoire
a350.name: Kadidiata Diarra Badji
a350.title: Director of Examinations and Competitions (DECO), Cote d'Ivoire
a350.speech: Expressed satisfaction at the smooth running of the examinations: "As for the CEPE, no major incident likely to compromise the credibility of the examinations was reported in the various examination centres."

a350.speaker: Kadidiata Diarra Badji, Director of Examinations and Competitions (DECO), Cote d'Ivoire
a350.name: Kadidiata Diarra Badji
a350.title: Director of Examinations and Competitions (DECO), Cote d'Ivoire
a350.speech: "I recall and I insist on the fact that appeals and the issuing of transcripts of marks are entirely free of charge in all the centres," she specified.

a456.speaker: Peter Mutharika, former president of Malawi and leader of the opposition Democratic Progressive Party (DPP)
a456.name: Peter Mutharika
a456.title: former president of Malawi and leader of the opposition Democratic Progressive Party (DPP)
a456.speech: Encouraged Lhomwe people to diversify food choices and move away from reliance on maize to deal with perennial hunger in the Southern Region, saying that in the past Lhomwe people relied on crops such as pigeon peas, cassava, sweet potatoes and millet for food: “These crops are drought resistant as they do not require a lot of rain. Of course, we should grow maize but we need to move to these traditional foods to deal with perennial hunger.”

a456.speaker: Peter Mutharika, former president of Malawi and leader of the opposition Democratic Progressive Party (DPP)
a456.name: Peter Mutharika
a456.title: former president of Malawi and leader of the opposition Democratic Progressive Party (DPP)
a456.speech: Urged people to register [for the September 16 2025 General Elections] ; spoke against suicide, victimisation of girls, trafficking in persons and attacks against the elderly in the country ; noted that it is common in the Lhomwe belt districts such as Phalombe, Mulanje and Thyolo for people to send children to Mozambique to work in farms: “I appeal to chiefs and all community leaders to ensure that the culture of sending children to other areas should stop.”

a456.speaker: Blessings Makwinja, representative of Lhomwe Paramount Chief Kaduya
a456.name: Blessings Makwinja
a456.title: representative of Lhomwe Paramount Chief Kaduya
a456.speech: Mentioned the continued rise in prices of goods and services, unemployment, natural disasters and hunger as some of the challenges that people are facing, and said people from the Lhomwe belt will register for the 2025 General Elections and vote massively on polling day as a way of resolving these challenges.

a456.speaker: Felix Tambulasi, organising committee chairperson and private practice lawyer
a456.name: Felix Tambulasi
a456.title: organising committee chairperson and private practice lawyer
a456.speech: Said they faced many challenges in raising funds because of the poor economic situation in the country: “Despite the challenges, various individuals and organisations contributed and we have raised K180 million which has been used to buy food and cover other costs for this event.”

a517.speaker: Mirjana Spoljaric, President of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC)
a517.name: Mirjana Spoljaric
a517.title: President of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC)
a517.speech: Warned Monday that failure to help Syria "get back on its feet" will result in a fresh wave of outward migration, saying the situation in the country is fragile, with outbursts of violence and the conflict's legacy of destruction making aid all the more indispensable: "When you don't have schools for your children, when you don't have functioning hospitals, when you don't have access to water and energy, when your house is still collapsed, and you don't have the means to rebuild (it), you will be forced to leave," she told AFP in an interview.

a517.speaker: Mirjana Spoljaric, President of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC)
a517.name: Mirjana Spoljaric
a517.title: President of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC)
a517.speech: "Syria is at the crossroads," Spoljaric said, adding that peace and stability were "possible" but required "a lot of attention" from the international community.

a517.speaker: Mirjana Spoljaric, President of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC)
a517.name: Mirjana Spoljaric
a517.title: President of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC)
a517.speech: Did not provide a figure but said she hoped the conference would produce funding and political commitment to help the new authorities rebuild "a functioning economy, which at the moment is not existent" ; "If we want people to be able to stay or to come back if they wish, we have to support them in building the environment that would allow them to live and live in a dignified way." ; she noted that the ICRC budget for Syria for 2025 is only about 14% funded so far.

a517.speaker: Mirjana Spoljaric, President of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC)
a517.name: Mirjana Spoljaric
a517.title: President of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC)
a517.speech: Said the ICRC, like others, has been impacted by President Donald Trump's decision to suspend US foreign aid, but that it is "engaging" with Washington to continue cooperation.

a517.speaker: Mirjana Spoljaric, President of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC)
a517.name: Mirjana Spoljaric
a517.title: President of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC)
a517.speech: Said money was needed, among other things, to support efforts to determine the fate of tens of thousands of detainees and others who went missing during the war: "The healing of a country cannot happen if the missing files are not resolved."

a517.speaker: United Nations
a517.name: United Nations
a517.speech: According to the United Nations, more than 300 000 refugees have returned to Syria, hoping to start over following the ouster of Bashar al-Assad.

a865.speaker: Constitution of the Republic of Cabo Verde (2010), Article 9
a865.name: Constitution of the Republic of Cabo Verde (2010)
a865.title: Article 9
a865.speech: States that “the State promotes the conditions for the officialisation of the Cape Verdean mother tongue, on a par with the Portuguese language.”

a865.speaker: Current Minister of Education of Cabo Verde
a865.name: Current Minister of Education of Cabo Verde
a865.speech: In an interview with Expresso das Ilhas (March 2025), said that it is necessary to “give time to time” and referred to Portuguese as an “equally identity-forming language.”

a894.speaker: Advocacy for Disability Act Cluster (ADAC)
a894.name: Advocacy for Disability Act Cluster (ADAC)
a894.speech: Commended the Taraba State House of Assembly for the second reading of the Taraba State Disability Bill, aimed at establishing a commission for persons with disabilities.

a894.speaker: Grace Jerry, ADAC Cluster Anchor and Executive Director of The Inclusive Friends Association (IFA)
a894.name: Grace Jerry
a894.title: ADAC Cluster Anchor and Executive Director of The Inclusive Friends Association (IFA)
a894.speech: Noted in a statement that this significant legislative step, led by Speaker RT Hon. John Kizito Bonzena, reflects a commitment to inclusivity under Governor Agbu Kefas ; declared that the Assembly’s actions mark a pivotal move towards an inclusive state, expressing excitement that the governor, His Excellency Agbu Kefas, will make the community of Persons with Disabilities in Taraba proud by assenting to the Bill as soon as the Assembly is through with their Legislative process.

a894.speaker: ADAC and other civil society organisations
a894.name: ADAC and other civil society organisations
a894.speech: Expressed support for the bill, emphasizing its potential to enhance education, healthcare, and civil rights for over half a million individuals with disabilities in Taraba.

a894.speaker: Advocacy for Disability Act Cluster (ADAC) statement
a894.name: Advocacy for Disability Act Cluster (ADAC) statement
a894.speech: “The Advocacy for Disability Act (ADAC), a consortium of five Civil Society Organizations (CSO)... Implementing the Strengthening Civic Advocacy and Local Engagement (SCALE) through Palladium funded by USAID joins the Joint Association of Persons with Disability (JONPWD) Taraba State Chapter, and other CSOs in Taraba state, applauds the Taraba State House of House Assembly for being an inclusive Legislature on the occasion of the second reading of the A Bill to establish the Taraba State Persons With Disabilities Commission under the leadership of the Speaker RT Hon. John Kizito Bonzena” ; “The reality of the Second reading and the fixing of Thursday, October 24, 2024, demonstrate high integrity on the part of the Assembly and a demonstration in line with the inclusivity nature of His Executive Governor, His Excellency Agbu Kefas who has demonstrated passion for the community of Persons with Disabilities since he assumes office” ; “The direction of the Taraba Assembly in ensuring policies and legislation that protect the Disability Community is no doubt the right step in the right direction as it provides an avenue for sustained implementation of education, healthcare, social, economic, and civil rights on right base issues other the charity model approach” ; “The ADAC Cluster joins the population of over half a million Persons with Disabilities in Taraba State to applaud this laudable step and the courage of Hon. Annas Shua’abu for sponsoring the Bill and other members who believed and supported the course” ; “While we commend the efforts of the House Committee on Social Welfare in coordination with the Public Hearing, we encourage the Media and CSOs to make informed contributions that will drive a credible process toward a holistic document” ; “The ADAC is proud to be part of this process and encouraged that the Taraba State Assembly continue in this professional and people-oriented legislative leadership towards achieving inclusive legislation that will further help harness the potential of the disability community in Taraba State.”

a894.speaker: Hon. Jethro Yakubu Zikengyu, Member representing Wukari I constituency and Majority Leader of the Taraba State House of Assembly
a894.name: Hon. Jethro Yakubu Zikengyu
a894.title: Member representing Wukari I constituency and Majority Leader of the Taraba State House of Assembly
a894.speech: Alongside other members of the Assembly present, “had committed at the occasion of the retreat that, the Disability Law will become a reality in Taraba state.”

a948.speaker: Muse Bihi, Somaliland President
a948.name: Muse Bihi
a948.title: Somaliland President
a948.speech: At the launch event: “I would like to thank the UK and partners for their role in investing in Somaliland's infrastructure to boost the economy, which will help in service delivery as well as create employment.”

a948.speaker: Kate Foster, UK Ambassador to Somalia
a948.name: Kate Foster
a948.title: UK Ambassador to Somalia
a948.speech: “We are proud to support the Hargeisa bypass, which is a crucial part of the Berbera corridor. Once this 240 km project – in coordination with our Abu Dhabi and European partners – is completed late next year, it will improve the lives of hundreds of thousands of people by creating jobs, unlocking the region's economic potential and ease the delivery of humanitarian supplies.” ; “At a time of huge challenges for Somaliland, including tackling COVID-19, this is a demonstration of the UK's commitment to the people of Somaliland.”

a948.speaker: Eugene Torero, Director of Trade Policy at TradeMark East Africa
a948.name: Eugene Torero
a948.title: Director of Trade Policy at TradeMark East Africa
a948.speech: “We are grateful for the continued support by United Kingdom and the fruitful partnership with the Somaliland government which has ensured steady progress in the construction of this important road amidst many challenges.” ; “TMEA is committed to continue implementing various initiatives, with the government, that will support Somaliland's agenda in increasing trade not only within its borders but also with its neighbours consequently creating jobs and helping reduce poverty.”

a1075.speaker: New leaders of Syria
a1075.name: New leaders of Syria
a1075.speech: Recently reiterated requests for aid to the Gulf countries to rebuild the country devastated by more than 13 years of war.

a1117.speaker: UN humanitarian agency / World Food Programme (WFP)
a1117.name: UN humanitarian agency / World Food Programme (WFP)
a1117.speech: According to the UN humanitarian agency, more than 36 million people are "struggling to meet their food needs", a number that could rise to 52 million people this summer, during the lean season between two harvests, "including almost three million in emergency situations", according to the WFP.

a1117.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP) (communiqué)
a1117.name: World Food Programme (WFP) (communiqué)
a1117.speech: "Persistent conflicts, population displacements, the deteriorating economic situation and recurrent extreme weather conditions in West and Central Africa are pushing millions of people into emergency levels of hunger," the statement reads.

a1117.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP)
a1117.name: World Food Programme (WFP)
a1117.speech: At the end of March, the UN agency spoke of an "unprecedented crisis" due to a 40% cut in its funding for 2025. At the end of April, the WFP announced that it would have to reduce its workforce by 25 to 30% worldwide. "Five million people risk being deprived of vital food assistance if urgent funding is not received," the organisation warned.

a1117.speaker: Margot van der Velden, WFP Regional Director for West and Central Africa
a1117.name: Margot van der Velden
a1117.title: WFP Regional Director for West and Central Africa
a1117.speech: "We are at a critical moment where millions of lives are at stake," she said. "Without immediate funding, WFP will be forced to further reduce the number of people it feeds and the size of the food rations it distributes," she stressed.

a1294.speaker: White House official (anonymous)
a1294.name: White House official (anonymous)
a1294.speech: told CNN that the meeting is intended to "explore commercial opportunities that benefit both the American people and our African partners."

a1294.speaker: Professor Christopher Afoke Isike, scholar of African international relations at the University of Pretoria
a1294.name: Professor Christopher Afoke Isike
a1294.title: scholar of African international relations at the University of Pretoria
a1294.speech: "This is not engagement—it's cherry-picking. Trump is targeting countries that are either politically pliable or rich in resources, and avoiding those that assert themselves independently or align with powers like China or Russia."

a1294.speaker: Observers/analysts
a1294.name: Observers/analysts
a1294.speech: note that the five invitees are neither continental heavyweights nor major players in pan-African politics; what they do have in common is untapped mineral wealth, strategic Atlantic access, and growing migration flows to the US—factors that fit neatly into Trump's foreign policy agenda. Analysts believe Trump is seeking to counter China's dominant trade and investment footprint across Africa through targeted partnerships.

a1294.speaker: Mamadou Thior, Dakar-based journalist who covered the first US–Africa Leaders' Summit in 2014
a1294.name: Mamadou Thior
a1294.title: Dakar-based journalist who covered the first US–Africa Leaders' Summit in 2014
a1294.speech: said the nature of Trump's engagement is unmistakable: "Trump is not looking for partners—he's looking for deals. And only with countries he believes he can control."

a1294.speaker: Lilongwe-based political analyst (anonymous)
a1294.name: Lilongwe-based political analyst (anonymous)
a1294.speech: "This kind of exclusion should be a wake-up call. If Malawi wants to be taken seriously, it needs to do more than just show up at donor forums. It needs a clear, assertive strategy on global partnerships, trade, and diplomacy."

a1294.speaker: Analysts
a1294.name: Analysts
a1294.speech: warn that African nations left out of this new transactional order could find themselves increasingly isolated unless they reposition themselves, as the Trump administration moves away from traditional aid models—having already dismantled most of USAID programs in Africa.

a1391.speaker: Ministry of Economic Planning and Development Second Quarter Performance Report
a1391.name: Ministry of Economic Planning and Development Second Quarter Performance Report
a1391.speech: The report reflects that the mining and quarrying subsector experienced a combination of operational efficiency and demand issues from destination markets in the coal industry, that heightened external competition dampened local performance in the forestry subsector, and that subdued activity in the secondary sector stemmed mainly from poor performance of the manufacturing subsector: "Unfavourable market dynamics also placed downward pressure on production in the subsector. On the contrary, increased construction activity owing to ongoing and new projects, such as the Construction of the International Convention Centre (ICC), Lower Usuthu Irrigation Project (LUSIP II) and MR14 and MR21 (110kms) road, cushioned the overall decline in the secondary sector."

a1391.speaker: IMF, World Economic Outlook Update, July 2025 (cited in the report)
a1391.name: IMF
a1391.title: World Economic Outlook Update, July 2025 (cited in the report)
a1391.speech: The report reflects that global growth prospects have improved due to robust front-loading in international trade before the kick-in of US tariff increases, lower average effective tariff rates for most countries than previously announced by the USA, improvement in global financial conditions as well as fiscal expansions in some jurisdictions; global growth projections have been revised upwards to 3.0 per cent in 2025 and 3.1 per cent in 2026, with Sub-Saharan Africa projected at 4.0 per cent in 2025 and 4.3 per cent in 2026.

a1391.speaker: Ministry of Economic Planning and Development Second Quarter Performance Report (on credit to the private sector)
a1391.name: Ministry of Economic Planning and Development Second Quarter Performance Report (on credit to the private sector)
a1391.speech: The report reflects that total credit extended to the private sector was recorded at E21.463 billion, an 8.1 per cent growth, mainly attributable to a rise in credit extended to businesses, households and other sectors: "Similarly, the country's financial buffers, as measured by the gross official reserves, increased by 12.2 per cent compared to the same period in 2024 and amounted to E11.949 billion. This increase was on account of an inflow of the Southern African Customs Union (SACU) receipts at the beginning of July 2025. At this level, the reserves were sufficient to cover 2.9 months of imports, falling short of the internationally recommended threshold of 3 months."

a1468.speaker: United Nations
a1468.name: United Nations
a1468.speech: has called for rival governments running Libya to work together to rebuild the country after a devastating storm ; said the biggest challenge that the international community rendering support was faced with was the country's political situation.

a1468.speaker: Abdoulaye Bathily, Special Representative of the Secretary-General for Libya and head of the United Nations Support Mission in Libya (UNSMIL)
a1468.name: Abdoulaye Bathily
a1468.title: Special Representative of the Secretary-General for Libya and head of the United Nations Support Mission in Libya (UNSMIL)
a1468.speech: He said he was worried that "plans floated by different institutions and leaders for reconstruction run the risk of deepening the existing rift between the internationally recognised government and a rival administration in the east". For the sake of rebuilding, he said the two rival administrations should work together to come up with a detailed and working roadmap. "UNSMIL calls on all relevant Libyan national and local authorities and Libya's international partners to facilitate agreement on a unified and coordinated Libyan national mechanism to direct the recovery and reconstruction efforts and to ensure transparency and accountability," he said in a statement. He added that Storm Daniel has shown Libyans and the world the importance of peace for a country to move forward, and as such, they should "expedite negotiations on breaking the political stalemate".

a1468.speaker: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a1468.name: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a1468.speech: said of the 4 333 known deaths, 101 were healthcare workers.

a1468.speaker: Ahmed Zouiten, WHO representative in Libya
a1468.name: Ahmed Zouiten
a1468.title: WHO representative in Libya
a1468.speech: said their deaths would negatively impact the country's health sector. He said: "Storm Daniel hit Libya, which had already been facing a heavily disadvantaged health sector that's underfunded, with fewer health workers than needed and bad infrastructure." Zouiten said the WHO would continue to support the country's health sector with those who died in mind. "WHO will honour their memory by pursuing efforts to restore healthcare and continue their legacy of serving the vulnerable, saving lives, and keeping the community safe," he added.

a1517.speaker: Kevin Johnson-Azuara, Chief Marketing Officer at Nigerdock (statement)
a1517.name: Kevin Johnson-Azuara
a1517.title: Chief Marketing Officer at Nigerdock (statement)
a1517.speech: Said that during the official signing ceremony of the establishment, the Chief Executive Officer of Nigerdock, Maher Jarmakani, said that they were looking forward to a partnership that would advance innovation.

a1517.speaker: Maher Jarmakani, Chief Executive Officer of Nigerdock
a1517.name: Maher Jarmakani
a1517.title: Chief Executive Officer of Nigerdock
a1517.speech: "We are delighted to welcome Transocean Coatings Nigeria to our economic zone and look forward to a partnership that will significantly contribute to the advancement of innovation, commerce, and economic growth across the region" ; He added that Transocean FZE joins SIIFZ's growing portfolio of multi-sector entities, including maritime, logistics, finance, energy, and heavy industry.

a1517.speaker: Oliver Birkett, Chief Executive Officer of Transocean Coatings Nigeria
a1517.name: Oliver Birkett
a1517.title: Chief Executive Officer of Transocean Coatings Nigeria
a1517.speech: "With Transocean Coatings' presence in over 20 countries, our newest facility within SIIFZ's strategic location increases our global footprint and enables us to better serve our clients with increased efficiency and proximity. It also reinforces our dedication to the region's infrastructure and energy sectors and our long-term vision for business growth in Africa."

a1575.speaker: United Nations
a1575.name: United Nations
a1575.speech: Slashed its aid appeal to donors by over a third, saying it was now seeking $29 billion to support 114 million people amid what it described as the deepest funding cuts ever ; In a statement, the U.N. said its request prioritises, but does not replace, an earlier appeal for over $47 billion launched in December 2024 ; The previous U.N. humanitarian appeal was less than 13% funded nearly halfway through the year, the U.N. said.

a1575.speaker: Tom Fletcher, U.N. aid chief
a1575.name: Tom Fletcher
a1575.title: U.N. aid chief
a1575.speech: Said that the scale of donor retrenchment had been so large that it has been "forced into a triage of human survival." ; "The math is cruel, and the consequences are heartbreaking. Too many people will not get the support they need, but we will save as many lives as we can." ; "All we ask is one percent of what you chose to spend last year on war. But this isn't just an appeal for money – it's a call for global responsibility, for human solidarity, for a commitment to end the suffering."

a1575.speaker: Donald Trump, U.S. President
a1575.name: Donald Trump
a1575.title: U.S. President
a1575.speech: Has himself described his major cuts to foreign aid as "devastating."

a1865.speaker: Dr. Mohammed Amin Adam, Minister of Finance of Ghana
a1865.name: Dr. Mohammed Amin Adam
a1865.title: Minister of Finance of Ghana
a1865.speech: Says his outfit expects the cedi's stability to improve into the medium-term as the government completes debt restructuring and also makes more progress on fiscal consolidation, and improves the country's reserves over the medium-term ; "We expect the cedi's stability to improve into the medium-term as we complete debt restructuring, make more progress on fiscal consolidation, and improve our reserves over the medium-term."

a1865.speaker: Dr. Mohammed Amin Adam, Minister of Finance of Ghana
a1865.name: Dr. Mohammed Amin Adam
a1865.title: Minister of Finance of Ghana
a1865.speech: Attributed the current pressures on the Cedi to the "strengthening of the US Dollar against major trading currencies": "The recent pressures we are observing on the cedi is largely on the back of the strengthening of the US Dollar against major trading currencies, seasonal forex demand including elevated demand from corporate institutions, payment to contractors and to IPPs, high Cedi liquidity and speculation."

a1865.speaker: Dr. Mohammed Amin Adam, Minister of Finance of Ghana
a1865.name: Dr. Mohammed Amin Adam
a1865.title: Minister of Finance of Ghana
a1865.speech: Addressing the media at his monthly press briefing on the economy, stated that the depreciation of the Cedi has been largely stabilised from November 2022 to December 2023 and continues to experience a fair appreciation against the Dollar in 2024, explaining that the depreciation of the cedi against the US Dollar halved from 54.2% at the end of Nov 2022 to 27.8% at the end of Dec 2023: "But for recent pressures we are seeing on exchange rate movements, the exchange rate has been largely stabilised with the depreciation of the cedi against the US Dollar halving from 54.2% at the end of Nov 2022 to 27.8% at the end of Dec 2023. The Cedi's stability has continued into 2024, with a cumulative depreciation of 14.2% as of 20th May 2024, compared to 20.7% recorded in the same period in 2023."

a1865.speaker: Dr. Mohammed Amin Adam, Minister of Finance of Ghana
a1865.name: Dr. Mohammed Amin Adam
a1865.title: Minister of Finance of Ghana
a1865.speech: Enumerated a number of measures including enhancing revenue mobilisation, approval of World Bank loans, among others which he said the government is working on to further improve the strength of the Cedi against some major trading currencies.

a1908.speaker: Taye Astqesellasie, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Ethiopia
a1908.name: Taye Astqesellasie
a1908.title: Minister of Foreign Affairs of Ethiopia
a1908.speech: "I'm not here to be insulted, man." — responded to a protestor who heckled him last week inside an international venue in Geneva, Switzerland, at a meeting called for pledges to raise funds from the international community to pay for emergency humanitarian assistance for millions of displaced Ethiopians due to drought, floods, conflicts and wars.

a1954.speaker: Damara Council and Damara United Front
a1954.name: Damara Council and Damara United Front
a1954.speech: Have jointly expressed their wish for elections for a Damara representative body that would be representative of all Damaras in Damaraland and in the other parts of South West Africa; they expressed this wish in talks held in Uis with Dirk Mudge, MEC, and a corresponding proposal will be submitted to the Minister of Bantu Administration and Development.

a1954.speaker: Captain Vasco Lourenço (statement)
a1954.name: Captain Vasco Lourenço (statement)
a1954.speech: According to a statement by Captain Vasco Lourenço, the plan or enabling pact of the Revolutionary Military Movement is to be signed next Friday at a public ceremony; Captain Lourenço also announced a tribunal for the unsuccessful right-wing putschists, before which 140 military personnel and 20 civilians await charges.

a1954.speaker: Observers
a1954.name: Observers
a1954.speech: Believe that the air attack on the presidential palace was a revenge attack by the pilot, Lieutenant Trung, whose family was not included in the evacuation of Da Nang and fell into communist hands.

a1954.speaker: Gerald Ford, President of the United States
a1954.name: Gerald Ford
a1954.title: President of the United States
a1954.speech: Maintained an optimistic stance on the situation in South Vietnam.

a1954.speaker: General F. Weyand, US Chief of Staff
a1954.name: General F. Weyand
a1954.title: US Chief of Staff
a1954.speech: Gave a positive assessment: “The South Vietnamese troops are still strong and have the fighting spirit and the ability to defeat the Vietcong.”

a1954.speaker: Diplomatic observers
a1954.name: Diplomatic observers
a1954.speech: Believe that President Nguyen Van Thieu could strengthen his weakened position again after the failed attempt on his life.

a1954.speaker: Marshal Ky, political rival of Van Thieu
a1954.name: Marshal Ky
a1954.title: political rival of Van Thieu
a1954.speech: Did not favour a violent overthrow of the president, saying that would only benefit the communists.

a1954.speaker: The Vietcong
a1954.name: The Vietcong
a1954.speech: Reported that the attempt on the President’s life proves how hated he is among the Vietnamese people.

a1954.speaker: Nguyen Van Thieu, President of South Vietnam
a1954.name: Nguyen Van Thieu
a1954.title: President of South Vietnam
a1954.speech: Declared in a radio address that he was determined to continue to carry out his office; he said that one group was demanding his resignation and that the bombing had been an isolated attempt to overthrow a constitutional and legal regime, and that two coup attempts had already been foiled in recent weeks.

a1954.speaker: S. L. Muller, Minister of Transport
a1954.name: S. L. Muller
a1954.title: Minister of Transport
a1954.speech: Declared in the House of Assembly that it was not the government’s intention to make the wearing of seat belts in motor vehicles a legal obligation, and that the provincial administration could take a different position.

a1954.speaker: J. T. Kruger, Minister of Justice
a1954.name: J. T. Kruger
a1954.title: Minister of Justice
a1954.speech: Announced that the government does not intend to abolish the death penalty.

a1954.speaker: K. D. Matanzima, Chief Minister of the Transkei
a1954.name: K. D. Matanzima
a1954.title: Chief Minister of the Transkei
a1954.speech: Described the students of the Federal Theological Seminary in Umtata as a threat to the security of the Transkei, saying that according to a document that was found, “religious training” apparently includes revolt against the existing order.

a1977.speaker: Office of the Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a1977.name: Office of the Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a1977.speech: Unveiled a three-year economic reform plan dubbed the "Homegrown Economic Reform Programme."

a1977.speaker: James Carville, Bill Clinton's campaign strategist
a1977.name: James Carville

a1977.speaker: Macroeconomic and policy advisors to Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed
a1977.name: Macroeconomic and policy advisors to Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed

a1977.speaker: IMF Chief Economist

a1977.speaker: International Monetary Fund (global growth outlook)

a2002.speaker: Anita Borg Institute (ABIE), a US-based organisation committed to promoting women in ICT
a2002.name: Anita Borg Institute (ABIE)
a2002.title: a US-based organisation committed to promoting women in ICT
a2002.speech: awarded Violette Uwamutara, Country Director of Digital Opportunity Trust (Dot), during the 2013 Grace Hopper Celebration of Women in Computing, recognising her for being a leading role model who is advancing the participation of Rwandan women in technology and introducing them to new opportunities and careers in the field of technology and entrepreneurship.

a2180.speaker: Malawi Congress Party (MCP) election manifesto
a2180.name: Malawi Congress Party (MCP) election manifesto
a2180.speech: has unveiled its manifesto for the September 16 General Election, with focus on food security, job creation, wealth creation, governance reforms and improved public service delivery, promising three million jobs for the youth in half a decade, a K500 000 investment account for every child and scaled-up social protection.

a2180.speaker: Dalitso Kubalasa, economic policy analyst
a2180.name: Dalitso Kubalasa
a2180.title: economic policy analyst
a2180.speech: On whether the pledges are realistic: "Gauging by our immediate past, any of these promises is simply not going to happen without a serious shift from political promises to real fiscal responsibility and integrity. The last five years have been filled with more talk than action. The economy is under pressure, donor confidence is shaky and public trust has eroded. Stretching an already fragile public budget with ambitious pledges risks deepening the crisis."

a2180.speaker: Dalitso Kubalasa, economic policy analyst
a2180.name: Dalitso Kubalasa
a2180.title: economic policy analyst
a2180.speech: On whether the programmes are necessary: "Absolutely. But they need a total makeover. What Malawi truly needs are focused, transparent and sustainable strategies. Sweeping populist promises without strong delivery systems, adequate funding and accountability mechanisms only feed disillusionment. Transformation requires more than excitement. It requires strategy and systems that work."

a2180.speaker: Dalitso Kubalasa, economic policy analyst
a2180.name: Dalitso Kubalasa
a2180.title: economic policy analyst
a2180.speech: On affordability: "Not at this rate. Malawi is grappling with an aid freeze, rising debt now over K17 trillion and sluggish growth in domestic revenue. Without growing our revenue base and plugging financial leakages, these promises become dangerously hollow. Fiscal space is tightening, and the cost of borrowing is rising. We're running out of room for error."

a2180.speaker: Dalitso Kubalasa, economic policy analyst
a2180.name: Dalitso Kubalasa
a2180.title: economic policy analyst
a2180.speech: On the impact on core development priorities: "There is a serious risk that essential reforms will be sidelined. Politicised spending tends to crowd out investment in areas where long-term transformation begins. If we keep leaning towards populism, sectors like education infrastructure, governance reform and health services will continue to suffer neglect."

a2180.speaker: Dalitso Kubalasa, economic policy analyst
a2180.name: Dalitso Kubalasa
a2180.title: economic policy analyst
a2180.speech: On what the next government should do differently: "First, it must merge ambition with action. Malawi has a clear vision in the form of Malawi 2063, but the problem lies in execution. We need the courage to prioritise what is truly sustainable and the honesty to drop what is not. This means moving from political theatre to fiscal discipline, and from dependency to citizen-led change."

a2180.speaker: Dalitso Kubalasa, economic policy analyst
a2180.name: Dalitso Kubalasa
a2180.title: economic policy analyst
a2180.speech: On specific reform steps: recommended eight urgent actions - speaking the truth rather than fantasy and confronting a broken public service, a youth bulge with no jobs and a crushing debt burden; building a national reform coalition involving youth leaders, civil society, churches, private sector players and development partners; crafting a smart, localised vision with job-focused youth innovation hubs, performance-based bursaries and community-driven development funds; mobilising citizens for reform; fixing the leaks by rooting out ghost beneficiaries and procurement abuses; generating quick wins by piloting success stories in selected districts and monitoring every kwacha spent; acting through crisis rather than after, with a dedicated delivery unit; and changing the culture so that public service is restructured around integrity and results.

a2180.speaker: Dalitso Kubalasa, economic policy analyst
a2180.name: Dalitso Kubalasa
a2180.title: economic policy analyst
a2180.speech: Final thoughts ahead of the polls: "Malawi doesn't need more catchy phrases. We need a fresh, grounded approach. The next government must understand that real transformation is quiet, consistent and accountable. Let's focus on fewer promises and more delivery. The public is no longer impressed by drama. They want results."

a2195.speaker: Donald Trump, US President (executive order of 20 January)
a2195.name: Donald Trump
a2195.title: US President (executive order of 20 January)
a2195.speech: "The United States foreign aid industry and bureaucracy are not aligned with American interests and in many cases are contrary to American values. They serve to destabilise world peace by promoting in foreign countries ideas that are directly opposed to harmonious and stable relations within and between countries." Such is the conviction of Donald Trump that motivates the suspension of American aid. Consequently, he indicated, the policy of the United States is that no further foreign aid will be disbursed in a manner that is not fully consistent with the foreign policy of the President of the United States.

a2195.speaker: Donald Trump, US President (executive order of 20 January)
a2195.name: Donald Trump
a2195.title: US President (executive order of 20 January)
a2195.speech: Decrees a 90-day pause in United States foreign development assistance to assess the effectiveness of programmes and their consistency with American foreign policy; instructs all department and agency heads responsible for United States foreign development assistance programmes to immediately suspend new obligations and disbursements of development aid funds to foreign countries, implementing non-governmental organisations, international organisations and contractors pending review; indicates in his order that the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) must enforce this pause through its apportionment authority.

a2195.speaker: Donald Trump, US President (executive order of 20 January)
a2195.name: Donald Trump
a2195.title: US President (executive order of 20 January)
a2195.speech: "New obligations and disbursements of foreign development assistance funds may resume for a programme before the end of the 90-day period if a review is carried out and if the Secretary of State or his designee, in consultation with the Director of the OMB, decides to continue the programme in the same or a modified form. In addition, any other new foreign assistance programme and obligation must be approved by the Secretary of State or his designee, in consultation with the Director of the OMB."

a2247.speaker: Professor Sagir Adamu Abbas, Vice Chancellor of Bayero University Kano (BUK)
a2247.name: Professor Sagir Adamu Abbas
a2247.title: Vice Chancellor of Bayero University Kano (BUK)
a2247.speech: Commended the former students for their unwavering commitment to the annual donation aimed at supporting undergraduates ; encouraged other alumni groups and related organizations to emulate the noble gesture, emphasizing the importance of collective efforts in fostering education and providing opportunities for underprivileged students.

a2247.speaker: Muhammad Dahiru Sa'ad, Chairman of BUK Class '92
a2247.name: Muhammad Dahiru Sa'ad
a2247.title: Chairman of BUK Class '92
a2247.speech: "This is a yearly event where we reconnect and engage with our alma mater. We met the Vice Chancellor and presented N2 million to support indigent students." ; "We allocated N1.2 million to 15 patients needing urgent medical attention at the teaching hospital. We identify those in critical conditions and provide assistance. This marks the ninth consecutive year of reunion meetings, engagement and collaboration." ; "Our collective efforts make a meaningful impact and drive progress; we hope to sustain it. Many members have suggested potential areas for investment to make our contributions for the university and the community more sustainable."

a2247.speaker: Engr. Rakiya Abubakar, Vice Chairperson, Abuja Chapter of BUK '92
a2247.name: Engr. Rakiya Abubakar
a2247.title: Vice Chairperson, Abuja Chapter of BUK '92
a2247.speech: Stressed the importance of regular gatherings and urged members in other states to establish similar chapters to enhance networking as well as humanitarian assistance.

a2247.speaker: Yushau Shuaib, Managing Director of Image Merchants Promotion Limited (IMPR), publishers of PRNigeria and Economic Confidential
a2247.name: Yushau Shuaib
a2247.title: Managing Director of Image Merchants Promotion Limited (IMPR), publishers of PRNigeria and Economic Confidential
a2247.speech: Recognized the collective contributions of alumni members toward societal and human capital development: "I commend those among us who have extended support beyond alumni activities, such as helping other families and communities. Many are effectively using their positions for the greater good."

a2256.speaker: Institute for Women's Health (IWH)
a2256.name: Institute for Women's Health (IWH)
a2256.speech: Says the project aims to offer "evidence-based interventions to support the health and wellbeing of women and their families".

a2256.speaker: Senior source in the Ugandan health ministry (anonymous)
a2256.name: Senior source in the Ugandan health ministry (anonymous)
a2256.speech: Said one of Protego's more ambitious goals is to roll out clinics that deliver a significant range of reproductive health services to women, as well as cancer screenings.

a2256.speaker: The Bureau of Investigative Journalism (TBIJ)
a2256.name: The Bureau of Investigative Journalism (TBIJ)
a2256.speech: Can reveal that Huber and her charity, the IWH, have entered into a secretive agreement with the Ugandan government to find public money to spend on her Protego programme, and that key documents relating to the project are being kept away from the public eye.

a2256.speaker: One study (of Ohio's abstinence-only education programme)
a2256.name: One study (of Ohio's abstinence-only education programme)
a2256.speech: Found the state's abstinence-only education programme to contain "false and misleading information" under Huber's tenure.

a2256.speaker: Valerie Huber, former Trump administration official and head of the Institute for Women's Health (statement)
a2256.name: Valerie Huber
a2256.title: former Trump administration official and head of the Institute for Women's Health (statement)
a2256.speech: Said the IWH and the Protego project drew on "science-based concepts". She cited a number of studies which showed people undergoing abstinence education delayed their "sexual debut", were "no less likely to use a condom" and had "improved academic success".

a2256.speaker: Extensive research supported by major medical institutions / leading experts
a2256.name: Extensive research supported by major medical institutions / leading experts
a2256.speech: Has found abstinence-only education does not significantly delay the initiation of sexual activity in young people - it simply leaves them ill-informed and unprepared; some previous research has shown some young people in abstinence-based programmes are similarly likely to use condoms, but leading experts have criticised them for both withholding accurate information and including inaccurate information, as well as promoting harmful gender stereotypes.

a2256.speaker: Protego framework document (copy seen by TBIJ)
a2256.name: Protego framework document (copy seen by TBIJ)
a2256.speech: Mentions abstinence and "natural family planning" as well as modern evidence-based methods, and states any discussion of contraception should include education about avoiding "sexual risks".

a2256.speaker: Gillian Kane, director of global policy at the reproductive rights charity Ipas
a2256.name: Gillian Kane
a2256.title: director of global policy at the reproductive rights charity Ipas
a2256.speech: "There are existing programmes [in Uganda] that are vetted, they're implemented by professionals in the field," she said. "There are technicians who know how to provide health services." She said that Huber's project "really raises a lot of questions [about] their area of expertise and what they're replacing." ; said that people she has spoken to with access to Huber have been met by a "vacuum of detail about what it is".

a2256.speaker: Uganda's Ministry of Health
a2256.name: Uganda's Ministry of Health
a2256.speech: Told the TBIJ that Protego will supplement, not replace, existing services. It also said the concept of abstinence is "integral to Uganda's moral fabric" and has been used in the past to combat HIV transmission, as part of a strategy also involving contraception.

a2256.speaker: Institute for Women's Health (IWH)
a2256.name: Institute for Women's Health (IWH)
a2256.speech: Told the TBIJ the Protego framework is "culturally sensitive" to local populations and "does not force beliefs, values, or doctrines upon a country and its people".

a2256.speaker: Relevant Ugandan ministries, the Organisation of African First Ladies for Development and Huber's IWH (non-response)
a2256.name: Relevant Ugandan ministries
a2256.title: the Organisation of African First Ladies for Development and Huber's IWH (non-response)
a2256.speech: The TBIJ has repeatedly asked them to see the agreement and has made formal requests for information about what it contains, but with no success.

a2256.speaker: Sources in ministries working on the project and providers of reproductive health services in Uganda (anonymous)
a2256.name: Sources in ministries working on the project and providers of reproductive health services in Uganda (anonymous)
a2256.speech: Have told the TBIJ that Protego is being coordinated by the office of the first lady - which is also where key documents relating to the project are being held.

a2256.speaker: Constitutional lawyer familiar with the situation (anonymous)
a2256.name: Constitutional lawyer familiar with the situation (anonymous)
a2256.speech: Explained that the first lady's office does not have the same status in Uganda law as a government ministry and therefore cannot be scrutinised or challenged in the same way. He described the situation as "unconstitutional".

a2256.speaker: A commissioner in the Ugandan health ministry and a member of parliament who helped set up the project
a2256.name: A commissioner in the Ugandan health ministry and a member of parliament who helped set up the project
a2256.speech: Have confirmed to the TBIJ that there is an agreement to find the Protego money in some form from within the existing budgets of three government ministries.

a2256.speaker: Institute for Women's Health (IWH)
a2256.name: Institute for Women's Health (IWH)
a2256.speech: Said no money would be exchanged between the charity and other parties.

a2256.speaker: Dr Richard Mugahi, assistant commissioner at Uganda's Ministry of Health
a2256.name: Dr Richard Mugahi
a2256.title: assistant commissioner at Uganda's Ministry of Health
a2256.speech: Told the TBIJ that not all aspects of the plan may be able to go ahead within existing budgets. But asked whether there was a path to money coming in the future, he said: "Of course. Our chief mobiliser is the first lady, who is very passionate about this."

a2256.speaker: Sarah Opendi, member of parliament and chair of the Uganda Women Parliamentary Association
a2256.name: Sarah Opendi
a2256.title: member of parliament and chair of the Uganda Women Parliamentary Association
a2256.speech: Told the TBIJ she believes Protego should advocate abstinence for adolescents, rather than contraceptives, as a way to address the country's high teen pregnancy rate.

a2256.speaker: Dr Sabrina Kitaka, paediatrician who attended the launch event in May
a2256.name: Dr Sabrina Kitaka
a2256.title: paediatrician who attended the launch event in May
a2256.speech: Told the TBIJ she "did appreciate their vision and goal to support the girl child, to empower her, to make sure she doesn't become pregnant before she finishes school and also to promote women's health in general". But she added that "we have to not put our head in the sand" when it comes to the burden of teenage pregnancy and that contraception should be given to "those who need [it]".

a2256.speaker: Ophelia Kemigisha, activist and human rights lawyer
a2256.name: Ophelia Kemigisha
a2256.title: activist and human rights lawyer
a2256.speech: "The data shows that abstinence-only programmes do not work. A return to this strategy will lead to a loss of the progress made."

a2256.speaker: Project 2025 (document by the Heritage Foundation)
a2256.name: Project 2025 (document by the Heritage Foundation)
a2256.speech: Says the next administration should remove all references to "gender equality", "abortion" and "sexual and reproductive rights" from foreign aid policies, contracts and grants. It also recommends the removal of references to "controversial" sexual education materials.

a2256.speaker: Nana Darkoa Sekyiamah, co-founder of the Institute for Journalism and Social Change
a2256.name: Nana Darkoa Sekyiamah
a2256.title: co-founder of the Institute for Journalism and Social Change
a2256.speech: Told the TBIJ Huber's career and involvement in Project 2025 appeared to "point to her true agenda - to limit the sexual health and rights of girls, women and young people".

a2276.speaker: Thabo Chakaka Nyirenda, Attorney General of Malawi
a2276.name: Thabo Chakaka Nyirenda
a2276.title: Attorney General of Malawi
a2276.speech: Has hailed Zambia's legal framework on Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR), describing the Lusaka International Arbitration Centre as a testament to Zambia's political will towards ADR ; stating that the milestone is significant for ADR development in the SADC region.

a2276.speaker: Thabo Chakaka Nyirenda, Attorney General of Malawi
a2276.name: Thabo Chakaka Nyirenda
a2276.title: Attorney General of Malawi
a2276.speech: Emphasized that the success of a vibrant arbitration system relies on the quality implementation of arbitration laws, which requires a knowledgeable and skilled institution, including the judiciary and commercial bar. He further stressed the need for continuous training for both the judiciary and commercial bar. ; "There is no point in having arbitration laws merely on paper. Selecting the right methodology for implementing arbitration laws would make Malawi a suitable choice for commercial arbitration. I also admire my brother, State Counsel Kabesha's success in saving Zambia a whopping US$500 million, which ANTRA Energy claimed against ZESCO and the Zambian Government."

a2276.speaker: Thabo Chakaka Nyirenda, Attorney General of Malawi
a2276.name: Thabo Chakaka Nyirenda
a2276.title: Attorney General of Malawi
a2276.speech: Suggested that for Africa to become a preferred arbitral hub, there should be a consideration of Third Party Funding (TPF). ; However, he noted that African jurisdictions have varying approaches to TPF due to differing levels of legal development, economic priorities, and experience with arbitration.

a2276.speaker: Thabo Chakaka Nyirenda, Attorney General of Malawi
a2276.name: Thabo Chakaka Nyirenda
a2276.title: Attorney General of Malawi
a2276.speech: Highlighted Malawi's remarkable progress in harmonizing arbitration, including training nearly 200 lawyers from Malawi, Zambia, Zimbabwe, Namibia, and South Africa on international commercial arbitration. He pointed out the establishment of the Malawi International Arbitration Centre (MIAC), which was marked by a pre-launch conference in Lilongwe presided over by President Lazarus Chakwera, Chief Justice Rezine Mzikamanda, and Minister of Justice Titus Mvalo. ; Described the speed of the process as a testament to the concerted agreement among various stakeholders on the importance of having the MIAC.

a2276.speaker: Thabo Chakaka Nyirenda, Attorney General of Malawi
a2276.name: Thabo Chakaka Nyirenda
a2276.title: Attorney General of Malawi
a2276.speech: Urged stakeholders to consider reforms in modern arbitration laws, transforming outdated laws, strengthening judicial independence, enhancing legal expertise, upholding ethics, and ensuring the enforceability of arbitration agreements and awards. ; Assured Malawians of his office's continued support in providing necessary backing to the private sector and professional bodies interested in promoting ADR. He pledged to work tirelessly until the MIAC becomes fully functional.

a2278.speaker: Melanie Higgins, United States Ambassador to Burundi
a2278.name: Melanie Higgins
a2278.title: United States Ambassador to Burundi
a2278.speech: "Human trafficking occurs in countries that do not make sufficient efforts to combat this phenomenon." ; In her view, victims of trafficking must be supported and the perpetrators brought to justice. She calls on the national commission responsible for the prevention and suppression of trafficking in persons to give priority to the prosecution and conviction of the perpetrators of this crime.

a2278.speaker: Melanie Higgins, United States Ambassador to Burundi
a2278.name: Melanie Higgins
a2278.title: United States Ambassador to Burundi
a2278.speech: Hopes that Burundi will set up a national system for collecting data on the identification and protection of victims. In her view, a specific portion of the national budget must be devoted to funding activities to combat trafficking in persons. She recalls that in the annual report of the US department on trafficking in persons, Burundi moved up to Tier 2 of the watch list in 2021.

a2278.speaker: Jeroen Steeghs, Ambassador of the Kingdom of the Netherlands to Burundi
a2278.name: Jeroen Steeghs
a2278.title: Ambassador of the Kingdom of the Netherlands to Burundi
a2278.speech: Says trafficking in persons is a crime and a serious human rights violation of considerable magnitude. He deplores the fact that this crime often goes unnoticed: "Victims have a hard time talking about what happened to them. They are often threatened and blackmailed." ; According to him, about 66% of trafficking victims in Burundi are women and young girls, often destined for forced domestic labour, sexual violence and forced marriage, and are trafficked to neighbouring countries or to Gulf states.

a2278.speaker: Jeroen Steeghs, Ambassador of the Kingdom of the Netherlands to Burundi
a2278.name: Jeroen Steeghs
a2278.title: Ambassador of the Kingdom of the Netherlands to Burundi
a2278.speech: Recommends prevention, protection and the suppression of these crimes through an integrated approach in order to fight trafficking in persons effectively. In his view, effective actions must be implemented to protect victims and prosecute perpetrators.

a2278.speaker: Epitace Masumbuko, Chairman of the Burundian commission for consultation and monitoring on the prevention and suppression of trafficking in persons
a2278.name: Epitace Masumbuko
a2278.title: Chairman of the Burundian commission for consultation and monitoring on the prevention and suppression of trafficking in persons
a2278.speech: "The fight against trafficking in persons is a complex phenomenon that must involve several actors. It requires a multidisciplinary and intersectoral approach." ; He stresses that Burundi continues to record significant progress in the fight against trafficking in persons. In his view, the effectiveness of all stakeholders must be improved in order to further promote the protection of and assistance to victims of this crime.

a2278.speaker: Epitace Masumbuko, Chairman of the Burundian commission for consultation and monitoring on the prevention and suppression of trafficking in persons
a2278.name: Epitace Masumbuko
a2278.title: Chairman of the Burundian commission for consultation and monitoring on the prevention and suppression of trafficking in persons
a2278.speech: Explains that the standard operating procedures are detailed guidelines covering the identification, rescue, investigation, sheltering, return and reintegration of trafficking victims, and that they will improve the effectiveness of all stakeholders in protecting victims. He calls on all stakeholders to take ownership of them and implement them in order to align themselves with other countries in this fight.

a2278.speaker: Epitace Masumbuko, Chairman of the Burundian commission for consultation and monitoring on the prevention and suppression of trafficking in persons
a2278.name: Epitace Masumbuko
a2278.title: Chairman of the Burundian commission for consultation and monitoring on the prevention and suppression of trafficking in persons
a2278.speech: Regarding the recruitment of workers for the Gulf countries, he says that 17 recruitment companies already hold licences to operate in this field: "It is an initiative that forms part of the government's efforts to combat the root causes of trafficking in persons in Burundi."

a2356.speaker: Dambisa Moyo, author of the book Dead Aid
a2356.name: Dambisa Moyo
a2356.title: author of the book Dead Aid
a2356.speech: Discusses why aid does not really work in most African countries that are dependent on the West for survival, viewing the aid that comes to these countries as harmful because it perpetuates corruption and dependency, rather than promoting sustainable development and economic growth; observes that more than 50 years of aid from the West has not significantly developed Africa.

a2356.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a2356.name: Donald Trump
a2356.title: US President
a2356.speech: Has echoed Moyo sentiments and, among other things, has frozen aid provided through the US Agency for International Development (USaid), and has threatened to completely shut down USaid.

a2356.speaker: Government of Malawi
a2356.name: Government of Malawi
a2356.speech: Has said that it is looking for alternatives to USaid.

a2392.speaker: Bayo Onanuga, Special Adviser to the President on Information and Strategy (statement)
a2392.name: Bayo Onanuga
a2392.title: Special Adviser to the President on Information and Strategy (statement)
a2392.speech: Announced in a statement on Friday that President Bola Tinubu has appointed Mr. Ayo Sotinrin as the new Managing Director of the Bank of Agriculture, with immediate effect. The statement noted that Mr. Sotinrin is bringing a diverse and extensive background in the private and public sectors to his new role, and that before this appointment he held the position of Group Chief Executive Officer at the SAO Group: “His leadership at SAO Agro, an agribusiness company, was marked by groundbreaking agricultural initiatives, including developing a 20,000-hectare oil palm plantation and large-scale poultry, aquaculture, maize, and cassava operations in Ondo State. He also led SAO Capital, raising over $750 million in infrastructure and development finance, including the landmark $200 million Akure Water Supply Project.”

a2392.speaker: The Presidency
a2392.name: The Presidency
a2392.speech: Said Sotinrin served as Special Adviser (Environment & Urban Development) to the Minister of State FCT from 2011 to 2015, and that “his international background includes roles at the Royal Bank of Scotland International, Deutsche Bank, and the UK Environment Agency.”

a2392.speaker: Bola Tinubu, President of Nigeria
a2392.name: Bola Tinubu
a2392.title: President of Nigeria
a2392.speech: “Mr Sotinrin’s proven ability to mobilise capital, innovate in agribusiness, and collaborate across sectors will be instrumental in repositioning the Bank of Agriculture as a catalyst for food security, sovereignty and rural prosperity,” President Tinubu emphasised.

a2562.speaker: EUTM MOZ Command Group
a2562.name: EUTM MOZ Command Group
a2562.speech: Provided an overview on EUTM MOZ’ roles, capabilities, mission, current activities and the main ongoing projects within the Headquarters and the three training camps located in Katembe, Chimoio and Mavalane; described to the committee how EUTM MOZ is contributing to the capability building of the Mozambican armed forces’ units, selected to compose future Quick Reaction Forces (QRF).

a2562.speaker: EUTM Mozambique (@EUTMMozambique), Twitter post, July 14, 2023
a2562.name: EUTM Mozambique (@EUTMMozambique)
a2562.title: Twitter post, July 14, 2023
a2562.speech: “#EUTMMOZ welcomed the @CommonsForeign to the Katembe Training Camp. It was a useful opportunity to describe the committee how EUTM MOZ is contributing to the capability building of the Armed Forces’ units, selected to compose Quick Reaction Forces.”

a2754.speaker: Amanda Jacobsen, U.S. Deputy Chief of Mission
a2754.name: Amanda Jacobsen
a2754.title: U.S. Deputy Chief of Mission
a2754.speech: Highlighted that in Botswana adolescents (10 to 19) and young persons (15 to 24) living with HIV are among the most vulnerable yet underserved populations in the HIV response compared to adult populations, and said they are hopeful that the Operation Triple Zero initiative would amend this concern as this group lags behind across the entire HIV treatment cascade ; Emphasised that Adolescents and Young People (AYP) living with HIV face challenges related to growing up with HIV infection, including stigma and discrimination, clinical complications, side effects of treatment, problems with long-term adherence to treatment, stress, anxiety and other mental health issues, while faced with the developmental tasks of this phase of life: “Disclosure of HIV diagnosis to others, including sexual partners, sexual and reproductive health decisions, academic performance with potentially long-term effects on employability, income and wellbeing are challenges this cohort of young people face,” she added ; Reiterated that the plan of this programme is to increase the number of adolescents who get their treatment well with no missed appointments and perhaps become virally suppressed: “We believe that this approach will lead to an increase in the number of adolescents who are comfortable disclosing their HIV status, and who successfully enrol in and continue ART care and take full ownership of their health care,” she said ; Added that in the fiscal year 2023-2024, a total amount of $467,000 was provided to UNICEF to support this initiative.

a2754.speaker: Tlotlo Moilwa, HIV activist and Master of Ceremonies
a2754.name: Tlotlo Moilwa
a2754.title: HIV activist and Master of Ceremonies
a2754.speech: Emphasised that they are hopeful that this will help curb discrimination against people living with HIV, as the initiative aims at encouraging young people to disclose their status and achieve the mandate of the programme; decried that discrimination is still rife in Botswana, which hinders many, especially young people, from accepting their status and taking their treatment accordingly.

a2754.speaker: Dr Joan Matji, UNICEF Representative
a2754.name: Dr Joan Matji
a2754.title: UNICEF Representative
a2754.speech: Said that the programme comes at a critical time when adolescents are falling behind regarding the 95-95-95 targets, and they must not be left behind: “We have reasons to be proud of Botswana's progress in its HIV response. From being one of the countries with the highest burdens of HIV in the world, Botswana has achieved and, in some targets, surpassed the UNAIDS 95-95-95 targets. Moreover, we have received the silver tier status for PMTCT,” she said ; “UNICEF is grateful to have young people that are ready to champion their needs to ensure their voices are amplified and heard at all levels. Young people are the cornerstone of the country's present and future. It is therefore our hope to continue to see them engage and communicate their needs to decision makers,” she added ; Said their research has proven that in Motokwe village, many children under five years of age miss vaccinations and adolescents miss their medical monthly check-ups and medication.

a2754.speaker: Botswana AIDS Impact Survey (BAIS V)
a2754.name: Botswana AIDS Impact Survey (BAIS V)
a2754.speech: According to BAIS V, 84.5 percent of young people aged 15 to 24 years living with HIV were aware of their status, 98.5 percent of those aware were on ART, and 91.6 percent of those on ART had viral load suppression.

a2773.speaker: Paul Kagame, President of the Republic of Rwanda and AU Chair
a2773.name: Paul Kagame
a2773.title: President of the Republic of Rwanda and AU Chair
a2773.speech: "Governments should surely be willing and able to increase domestic investment in healthcare. A good indicator of this is the progress we have made toward securing the financial health of the African Union and mobilising our own resources for joint priorities, such as the Peace Fund. We should be the first ones to contribute to efforts that directly benefit our people."

a2773.speaker: Moussa Faki Mahamat, AU Commission Chair
a2773.name: Moussa Faki Mahamat
a2773.title: AU Commission Chair
a2773.speech: "We set ambitious health targets for 2030: ending epidemics and achieving universal health coverage for all. But the reality is that without substantial increases in domestic investment, and a radical change in the way health is harmonised to domestic and continental priorities, we will soon lose any realistic chance of reaching these objectives. Member States and Africa's partners must reorient health spending and health systems to target the diseases across the life cycle that have the greatest measurable impact on mortality and human capital development. We have a responsibility to African citizens to increase our investments today and we must not turn our back on them."

a2773.speaker: Peter Sands, Executive Director of the Global Fund
a2773.name: Peter Sands
a2773.title: Executive Director of the Global Fund
a2773.speech: "I am tremendously inspired by this African-led initiative to boost investments in health across Africa. To end epidemics, strengthen health systems and deliver universal health coverage, we all have to step up our investments in health."

a2773.speaker: African leaders
a2773.name: African leaders
a2773.speech: Urged countries to increase efficiency in their health sectors.

a2773.speaker: World Health Organization (estimate)
a2773.name: World Health Organization (estimate)
a2773.speech: Estimates that efficiency improvements could unlock at least 20%, and as much as 40%, of current spending on health, creating significantly better outcomes.

a2773.speaker: African leaders and global partners
a2773.name: African leaders and global partners
a2773.speech: Noted that the return on investment from increased and improved health financing is remarkable - 9-20 times the level of investment. $30 per person can generate $100bn in economic gains five years later.

a2773.speaker: Sahle-Work Zewde, President of the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia
a2773.name: Sahle-Work Zewde
a2773.title: President of the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia
a2773.speech: Noted, "Africa needs transformational leadership. We must bring hope and opportunity to our people and offer them full and prosperous lives. Growing our continent will be impossible if we do not put significant investments in health."

a2773.speaker: Dr Seth Berkley, CEO of Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance
a2773.name: Dr Seth Berkley
a2773.title: CEO of Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance
a2773.speech: "Since 2000, more than 293 million children in Africa have been immunised thanks to Gavi support. While we know that governments across the continent face a range of competing, worthy priorities, it's inspiring to see so many choose to put the health of their population first. Gavi commends the African Union and the Government of Rwanda for their leadership in improving health outcomes for the continent and stands ready to support countries in their efforts towards building sustainable immunisation and health programmes to help ensure no child dies from a preventable disease."

a2773.speaker: Bill Gates, Co-Chair, Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation
a2773.name: Bill Gates
a2773.title: Co-Chair, Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation
a2773.speech: "The time to mobilise domestic resources for health is now. The nations of the African Union have set bold, ambitious targets. If governments increase their investments in health, not a decade from now, but immediately, we know it is possible to meet set targets. We can end the epidemics of AIDS, TB, and malaria. We can achieve universal health coverage and grow Africa's economy in the process."

a2773.speaker: Dr. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, Director-General, World Health Organization
a2773.name: Dr. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus
a2773.title: Director-General, World Health Organization
