a2773.speech: "Universal health coverage is not a luxury only rich countries can afford. All countries can make progress with the resources they have. The Addis Ababa Call to Action is a powerful commitment from African Union leaders to increase domestic financing for health, and to hold themselves accountable for that commitment."

a2780.speaker: Government of Lesotho
a2780.name: Government of Lesotho
a2780.speech: Says it is shocked by US President Donald Trump saying that "nobody has ever heard of" the southern African nation.

a2780.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a2780.name: Donald Trump
a2780.title: US President
a2780.speech: Addressing the US Congress, listed cuts made to what he said was wasteful expenditure: "Eight million dollars to promote LGBTQI+ in the African nation of Lesotho, which nobody has ever heard of."

a2780.speaker: Spokesperson for Lesotho's foreign affairs department
a2780.name: Spokesperson for Lesotho's foreign affairs department
a2780.speech: Told the BBC that Lesotho enjoyed "warm and cordial" relations with the US.

a2780.speaker: US government (data)
a2780.name: US government (data)
a2780.speech: According to the US government, the two countries traded goods worth $240m (£187m) in 2024, mostly exports from Lesotho to the US, in particular textiles and clothing.

a2780.speaker: Lejone Mpotjoane, Lesotho's Foreign Affairs Minister
a2780.name: Lejone Mpotjoane
a2780.title: Lesotho's Foreign Affairs Minister
a2780.speech: Said it was "shocking" to hear a head of state "refer to another sovereign state in that manner" ; "To my surprise, 'the country that nobody has heard of' is the country where the US has a permanent mission." ; "Lesotho is a member of the UN and of a number of other international bodies. And the US has an embassy here and [there are] a number of US organisations we've accommodated here in Maseru." ; He later told the AFP news agency: "We are not taking this matter lightly," adding that they would send an official protest letter to Washington.

a2780.speaker: Lesotho officials
a2780.name: Lesotho officials
a2780.speech: Dismissed Trump's remarks as "off the cuff" and a "political statement", adding that they were "uncalled-for" given the good relations between the two nations.

a2780.speaker: Kutloano Pheko, Lesotho foreign affairs spokesperson
a2780.name: Kutloano Pheko
a2780.title: Lesotho foreign affairs spokesperson
a2780.speech: "We maintain very warm and cordial relations with the US. They've got a mission in Maseru and we also have [one] in Washington," he told the BBC ; was unable to confirm Trump's comments on the funding that went to LGBTQ organisations, saying that as the money went directly to them, they would be best placed to comment.

a2780.speaker: Lejone Mpotjoane, Lesotho's Foreign Affairs Minister
a2780.name: Lejone Mpotjoane
a2780.title: Lesotho's Foreign Affairs Minister
a2780.speech: Confirmed that the country had been affected by Trump's sudden decision to pause aid funding to countries around the world ; but declined to criticise this decision, saying it was the US's "prerogative to cut aid if they want to".

a2780.speaker: Lesotho health ministry
a2780.name: Lesotho health ministry
a2780.speech: Told South African publication GroundUp in February that Lesotho is among those countries that benefited from Pepfar, with TB and HIV programmes among those receiving the critical funds.

a2907.speaker: United States Commission for International Religious Freedom (USCIRF), 2025 annual report
a2907.name: United States Commission for International Religious Freedom (USCIRF)
a2907.title: 2025 annual report
a2907.speech: Has urged the US government to designate Nigeria as a “Country of Particular Concern” (CPC) due to persistent religious violence and the government’s failure to protect religious minorities ; condemned Nigerian authorities for failing to prosecute perpetrators of religious violence, warning that this inaction fuels reprisals, deepens sectarian tensions, and weakens religious freedom.

a2907.speaker: USCIRF report (documented cases)
a2907.name: USCIRF report (documented cases)
a2907.speech: Cited continued attacks on religious communities by Boko Haram (JAS), Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP), and armed bandits, who operate with little resistance from security forces ; documented a January 2024 incident when suspected Boko Haram insurgents killed 14 people in Yobe State, including a local pastor; stated that in May 2024 an Al-Qaeda-linked Ansaru militant kidnapped 160 mostly Christian children in Niger State, killing eight before releasing the rest; said in August 2024 armed bandits raided Christian-majority areas in Benue State, killing at least 70 people and abducting 20 students; and explained that in November 2024 the extremist Lakurawa group, enforcing their interpretation of Shari’a, reportedly executed 15 people in Kebbi State.

a2907.speaker: Stephen Schneck, USCIRF Chair
a2907.name: Stephen Schneck
a2907.title: USCIRF Chair
a2907.speech: “In 2024, religious freedom conditions in Nigeria remained poor. Federal and state governments either tolerated religious violence or failed to respond adequately to extremist groups seeking to impose their interpretation of Islam on communities.”

a2907.speaker: USCIRF
a2907.name: USCIRF
a2907.speech: Warned that such political silence emboldens religious extremists and sends a troubling message that perpetrators will not face consequences ; condemned Nigeria’s harsh blasphemy laws, which impose up to two years’ imprisonment for insulting religion at the federal level ; criticised the suppression of indigenous religious practices, noting the Anambra State government’s July 2024 demolition of an indigenous shrine following pressure from Catholic bishops.

a2907.speaker: USCIRF (recommendations to the US Government)
a2907.name: USCIRF (recommendations to the US Government)
a2907.speech: Recommended the U.S. government take immediate diplomatic action, including redesignating Nigeria as a “Country of Particular Concern” under the International Religious Freedom Act; called for classifying Boko Haram and ISWAP as “Entities of Particular Concern”; demanded increasing support for Nigerian civil society organisations advocating religious freedom, and redirecting U.S. foreign aid toward conflict resolution, security sector reform, and law enforcement training; recommended pressuring Nigerian authorities to end impunity for religious violence and ensure justice for victims; and called on the U.S. Congress to investigate whether U.S. assistance to Nigeria has effectively reduced religiously motivated violence.

a2907.speaker: Five American Republican senators (29 June 2022 memo to Secretary of State Antony Blinken)
a2907.name: Five American Republican senators (29 June 2022 memo to Secretary of State Antony Blinken)
a2907.speech: “Given the abysmal state of religious freedom in Nigeria, it is incumbent upon you to reverse last year’s decision and redesignate the country as a CPC. The moment demands that you do so without delay” ; informed Mr Blinken that religious violence and intolerance directed toward Nigerian Christians has worsened in recent years, and said the Nigerian authorities also restrict and “crack down on religious minorities and detain individuals indefinitely on blasphemy-related charges.”

a2907.speaker: Chris Smith, Chairman of the US House Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on Africa
a2907.name: Chris Smith
a2907.title: Chairman of the US House Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on Africa
a2907.speech: Urged President Donald Trump to impose harsh sanctions on Nigeria over the killing of Christians and condemned former Secretary of State Blinken for reversing Nigeria’s CPC status in 2021 ; stated that the Nigerian government has failed to tackle religiously motivated persecution of Christians “despite religious freedom being enshrined as an essential human right in its Constitution” ; “The Nigerian legal framework supports pluralism at both federal and state levels, but glaring contradictions exist, especially with laws that criminalise blasphemy – some even carrying the death penalty.”

a2907.speaker: Bishop Mamza, Nigerian Bishop (cited by Chris Smith)
a2907.name: Bishop Mamza
a2907.title: Nigerian Bishop (cited by Chris Smith)
a2907.speech: Challenged Blinken and said Christian persecution is “more intense than ever.”

a2907.speaker: Genocide Watch (cited by Chris Smith)
a2907.name: Genocide Watch (cited by Chris Smith)
a2907.speech: Has called Nigeria “a killing field of defenceless Christians.”

a2907.speaker: Muhammadu Buhari, former President of Nigeria
a2907.name: Muhammadu Buhari
a2907.title: former President of Nigeria
a2907.speech: Confirmed that during his visit to the US in 2018 he was confronted by US President Donald Trump, during his first term in office, with the allegation of killing of Christians.

a2907.speaker: Nigerian Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs (statement)
a2907.name: Nigerian Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs (statement)
a2907.speech: Denied allegations of targeted killings of Christians in the country, said reports promoting the allegations were misleading and intended to pressure the United States into designating Nigeria a CPC, and described any attempt to portray these attacks as religious persecution as inaccurate and misleading: “While the federal government acknowledges the security challenges confronting the nation, it is imperative to clarify that these negative activities are not driven by religious bias, nor targeted against any particular religious group” ; noted that the government has deployed security forces, enhanced intelligence gathering, and strengthened community engagement: “To bring an end to such security challenges, both the Federal and State authorities have embarked on kinetic and non-kinetic methods and expedited the implementation of the national livestock plan. To this end, a Ministry of Livestock Development has been established, while a Special Adviser and Coordinator of Livestock Reforms has been appointed to find sustainable solutions to pastoral farming, with a view to ending contestations over land between farmers and pastoral herders” ; urged the international community to verify information carefully before drawing conclusions that might escalate tensions within Nigeria.

a2907.speaker: European Parliament (resolution RC-B10-0101/2025)
a2907.name: European Parliament (resolution RC-B10-0101/2025)
a2907.speech: Passed a resolution in February demanding Nigeria abolish its blasphemy laws and immediately release Yahaya Sharif-Aminu: “Blasphemy laws violate international human rights standards and contradict Nigeria’s constitutional guarantee of religious freedom.”

a2907.speaker: European Union
a2907.name: European Union
a2907.speech: Reported that Mr Sharif-Aminu’s health is deteriorating due to harsh detention conditions, malnutrition, and lack of medical care.

a2907.speaker: United Nations Working Group on Arbitrary Detention (statement)
a2907.name: United Nations Working Group on Arbitrary Detention (statement)
a2907.speech: Declared his imprisonment a violation of international human rights law, urging the Nigerian government to immediately secure his release.

a2907.speaker: Amnesty International
a2907.name: Amnesty International
a2907.speech: Reported that over 7,000 Christians were killed in Nigeria in 2023 alone.

a2907.speaker: Isa Sanusi, Director of Amnesty International Nigeria
a2907.name: Isa Sanusi
a2907.title: Director of Amnesty International Nigeria
a2907.speech: “The authorities’ failure to investigate and prosecute these crimes highlights a shocking neglect of their duty to protect citizens.”

a2907.speaker: Atiku Abubakar, former Vice President of Nigeria (social media post)
a2907.name: Atiku Abubakar
a2907.title: former Vice President of Nigeria (social media post)
a2907.speech: Initially called for the arrest of those responsible for the killing of Deborah Yakubu in a social media post but later deleted it after facing backlash from his northern supporters.

a3078.speaker: International Court of Justice (ICJ), the UN’s highest court
a3078.name: International Court of Justice (ICJ)
a3078.title: the UN’s highest court
a3078.speech: On Friday ordered Israel to keep the Rafah crossing open, in the far south of the Gaza Strip on the border with Egypt, essential for the entry of humanitarian aid but closed after the launch of the ground operation in early May; it also ordered the “immediate and unconditional release” of the hostages in Gaza.

a3078.speaker: Israel (government)
a3078.name: Israel (government)
a3078.speech: Defended itself, stating that it “has not carried out and will not carry out any military operation in the Rafah area” likely to “lead to the destruction of the Palestinian civilian population.”

a3078.speaker: Hamas (Palestinian Islamist movement)
a3078.name: Hamas (Palestinian Islamist movement)
a3078.speech: Welcomed the ICJ’s decision, but regretted that it was limited “only to Rafah.”

a3078.speaker: Oum Mohammad al-Ashqa, a Palestinian woman from Gaza City displaced by the violence in Deir al-Balah
a3078.name: Oum Mohammad al-Ashqa
a3078.title: a Palestinian woman from Gaza City displaced by the violence in Deir al-Balah
a3078.speech: “We hope that the ICJ’s decision will pressure Israel to put an end to this war of extermination,” she told the news agency France-Presse (AFP).

a3078.speaker: Mohammed Saleh, a refugee in Deir al-Balah in the centre of the Palestinian territory
a3078.name: Mohammed Saleh
a3078.title: a refugee in Deir al-Balah in the centre of the Palestinian territory
a3078.speech: “Israel is a State that considers itself above the law. That is why I do not believe that (...) the war can end in any way other than by force,” he also stressed to AFP.

a3078.speaker: Witnesses (Palestinian sources and AFP reporting teams)
a3078.name: Witnesses (Palestinian sources and AFP reporting teams)
a3078.speech: Reported air strikes and artillery fire in Khan Yunis (south) and in several neighbourhoods of Gaza City (north) in the early hours of today; according to witnesses, fighter jets and helicopters struck the Jabalia camp (north) and fired at targets near a power plant north of the Nousseirat camp (centre).

a3078.speaker: AFP count based on official Israeli data
a3078.name: AFP count based on official Israeli data
a3078.speech: More than 1,170 people, mostly civilians, were killed on 7 October when Hamas commandos infiltrated from the Gaza Strip; 252 people were also taken hostage in the Palestinian territory that day.

a3078.speaker: Israel (official figures)
a3078.name: Israel (official figures)
a3078.speech: According to Israel, 121 hostages remain held in Gaza, 37 of them dead, after a truce in November allowed the release of about a hundred of them.

a3078.speaker: Hamas Health Ministry
a3078.name: Hamas Health Ministry
a3078.speech: According to the Hamas Health Ministry, the Israeli army’s offensive has killed at least 35,857 people in the Palestinian territory, mostly civilians.

a3078.speaker: United Nations
a3078.name: United Nations
a3078.speech: According to the UN, around 800,000 people have fled Rafah in the last two weeks.

a3078.speaker: Martin Griffiths, UN humanitarian operations chief
a3078.name: Martin Griffiths
a3078.title: UN humanitarian operations chief
a3078.speech: “We are at a critical moment,” he summed up during the night.

a3078.speaker: Prosecutor of the International Criminal Court (ICC)
a3078.name: Prosecutor of the International Criminal Court (ICC)
a3078.speech: Earlier in the week requested the issuance of arrest warrants for alleged crimes committed in the Gaza Strip and in Israel against Hamas leaders and Israeli leaders, including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

a3078.speaker: Israeli government / a senior official (anonymous)
a3078.name: Israeli government / a senior official (anonymous)
a3078.speech: The Israeli government condemned the prosecutor’s announcement, but ordered its negotiators to “return to the negotiating table to obtain the return of the hostages,” according to a senior official.

a3078.speaker: French Presidency
a3078.name: French Presidency
a3078.speech: According to the French Presidency, the leaders discussed the implementation of the “two-State solution”, that is, a viable Palestinian State alongside Israel; they also debated the “levers that can be activated to achieve the reopening of all crossing points” to the Palestinian territory and examined how to “increase and deepen cooperation on humanitarian aid.”

a3078.speaker: Washington (US government)
a3078.name: Washington (US government)
a3078.speech: According to Washington, US chief diplomat Antony Blinken held talks with Benny Gantz, a member of Israel’s war cabinet, on new efforts to reach a ceasefire and reopen the Rafah terminal “as quickly as possible.”

a3201.speaker: Timothy Melaye, Head of Communications of GIABA
a3201.name: Timothy Melaye
a3201.title: Head of Communications of GIABA
a3201.speech: Stated at the opening ceremony, representing GIABA Director General Mr. Edwin W. Harris, that the event presents an opportunity to strengthen collaboration with the academia in their shared responsibility to address the twin problems of money laundering and terrorist financing (ML/TF).

a3201.speaker: Timothy Melaye, Head of Communications of GIABA
a3201.name: Timothy Melaye
a3201.title: Head of Communications of GIABA
a3201.speech: Noted that these crimes are significant obstacles to the development of the region, causing adverse impacts such as erosion of reputation, loss of foreign direct investment, poor infrastructural development, dwindling confidence, and distortions in political and financial systems ; Underscored that money laundering and terrorist financing have far-reaching implications for regional security and development.

a3201.speaker: GIABA research and typology studies (including reports on the trafficking of small arms and light weapons, the nexus between money laundering and insurgency, and studies on tax fraud)
a3201.name: GIABA research and typology studies (including reports on the trafficking of small arms and light weapons
a3201.title: the nexus between money laundering and insurgency, and studies on tax fraud)
a3201.speech: Cited by Melaye as providing critical insights into the evolving nature of ML/TF threats and informing strategies to mitigate their impact.

a3201.speaker: Timothy Melaye, Head of Communications of GIABA
a3201.name: Timothy Melaye
a3201.title: Head of Communications of GIABA
a3201.speech: Stressed the need for sustained efforts despite significant progress made by member states in implementing AML/CFT regimes ; Explained that the implementation of AML/CFT standards within West Africa poses unique challenges and requires collective, concerted, and coordinated efforts at all levels ; Highlighted the dynamic nature of the criminal world, which necessitates adaptive and collaborative strategies to address emerging threats effectively.

a3201.speaker: Timothy Melaye, Head of Communications of GIABA
a3201.name: Timothy Melaye
a3201.title: Head of Communications of GIABA
a3201.speech: Said educational institutions play a pivotal role in the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, that academia has a critical role in addressing these menaces, and urged universities to integrate AML/CFT topics into their curricula, raise awareness within the academic community, and foster research on AML/CFT-related issues.

a3201.speaker: Timothy Melaye, Head of Communications of GIABA
a3201.name: Timothy Melaye
a3201.title: Head of Communications of GIABA
a3201.speech: Encouraged participants to take ownership of the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing through their commitment and motivation, and emphasised that while GIABA's efforts at the regional level are impactful, they require corresponding commitments at national and institutional levels ; Commended the participants for their dedication and encouraged them to remain advocates for AML/CFT efforts within their communities and beyond.

a3201.speaker: Timothy Melaye, Head of Communications of GIABA
a3201.name: Timothy Melaye
a3201.title: Head of Communications of GIABA
a3201.speech: Highlighted that these efforts have contributed to improved governance, enhanced development, and strengthened security in several member states, but emphasised that the fight against ML/TF is an ongoing battle requiring robust support from national authorities, institutions, and the general public ; Called for heightened collaboration across all sectors, including academia, government, and civil society, reiterating that the success of GIABA's efforts depends on the active participation of all stakeholders and that the fight against ML/TF is not just a regional or institutional responsibility but a collective duty.

a3201.speaker: Amos Y. Boakai, Deputy Director General of Liberia's Financial Intelligence Agency (FIA)
a3201.name: Amos Y. Boakai
a3201.title: Deputy Director General of Liberia's Financial Intelligence Agency (FIA)
a3201.speech: Also spoke at the event, highlighting the importance of GIABA's work, reaffirming Liberia's commitment to combating ML/TF and noting that the FIA plays a vital role in implementing corrective measures to address these challenges ; Acknowledged that while the work of the FIA may not always make them system-friendly, it is a necessary part of the government's ARREST agenda, and assured the audience of the FIA's resolve to continue its efforts despite resistance from individuals who benefit from financial crimes at the expense of the broader population.

a3243.speaker: Wilmot J.M. Paye, Liberian Minister of Mines and Energy
a3243.name: Wilmot J.M. Paye
a3243.title: Liberian Minister of Mines and Energy
a3243.speech: Described the Mineral Survey Report as a significant milestone and predicted a new future for the country's development agenda, stating that the mining sector presents a perfect opportunity for growth ; noted that the findings will help to propel the country to new heights and future possibilities for development: "This should present us with an opportunity for growth. This is a significant step to boost the sector" ; noted that the survey will serve as a useful guide for the country in setting aside protected areas.

a3243.speaker: Wilmot J.M. Paye, Liberian Minister of Mines and Energy
a3243.name: Wilmot J.M. Paye
a3243.title: Liberian Minister of Mines and Energy
a3243.speech: Highlighted the role of China as a valuable partner in Liberia's geological information gathering efforts and noted that the handover is a testament of the elevation of the China-Liberia tie by President Joseph Nyuma Boakai: "China has proven to be one of Liberia's partners. It was our pledge to get Liberia's geological information," he asserted, as he also lauded other partners including the United Kingdom and the United States for their support over the years.

a3243.speaker: Jeremiah Kpan Koung, Vice President of Liberia
a3243.name: Jeremiah Kpan Koung
a3243.title: Vice President of Liberia
a3243.speech: Underscored the crucial contribution of the mineral sector to Liberia's economy, stressing that the sector does not only contribute significantly to the nation's GDP but is also the backbone of Liberia's exports: "With mineral resources contributing an impressive 52 percent to Liberia's GDP and accounting for 93 percent of its exports, we must harness this potential for sustainable development" ; "This is a monumental step for Liberia."

a3243.speaker: Jeremiah Kpan Koung, Vice President of Liberia
a3243.name: Jeremiah Kpan Koung
a3243.title: Vice President of Liberia
a3243.speech: Emphasized the need for responsible exploration and extraction to maximize returns and promote sustainable development, and expressed optimism that Liberia's mineral wealth would benefit its citizens directly, highlighting the potential for economic independence and reduced reliance on foreign aid: "Our nation's mineral wealth, if managed effectively, has the potential to transform Liberia and lift countless people out of poverty" ; asserted that local communities should be the primary beneficiaries of mining activities.

a3243.speaker: Jeremiah Kpan Koung, Vice President of Liberia
a3243.name: Jeremiah Kpan Koung
a3243.title: Vice President of Liberia
a3243.speech: Acknowledged the historical support from countries like the United States and the United Kingdom in advancing Liberia's mining industry, emphasizing the importance of building on these partnerships: "We remember those who have helped us, and we hope to build on those foundations."

a3243.speaker: Jeremiah Kpan Koung, Vice President of Liberia
a3243.name: Jeremiah Kpan Koung
a3243.title: Vice President of Liberia
a3243.speech: Noted that previous studies were either incomplete or outdated, underscoring the importance of up-to-date data for investors and policymakers: "For Liberia to thrive, we need current information that reflects our real potential" ; extended an invitation to local and international investors, arguing that the clarity provided by the new data could attract investors: "Liberia is open for business, and we have the resources to back it up."

a3243.speaker: Jeremiah Kpan Koung, Vice President of Liberia
a3243.name: Jeremiah Kpan Koung
a3243.title: Vice President of Liberia
a3243.speech: Acknowledged the environmental impact of mining and promised that the government would take steps to ensure sustainable practices, calling for responsible mining to protect Liberia's rich biodiversity; promised that the survey results would be used to bring more transparency to the mining sector, with clear guidelines and regulations: "We want to ensure that the wealth from our resources benefits the people of Liberia, not just a few."

a3243.speaker: Jeremiah Kpan Koung, Vice President of Liberia
a3243.name: Jeremiah Kpan Koung
a3243.title: Vice President of Liberia
a3243.speech: Expressed the government's gratitude to the People's Republic of China for its continued support and collaboration, and acknowledged China's contribution as a testament to Liberia's expanding partnerships and growing influence in the global mining industry.

a3285.speaker: 2018 Global Food Policy Report
a3285.name: 2018 Global Food Policy Report
a3285.speech: States that African countries should continue to monitor progress toward the Malabo Declaration on Accelerated Agricultural Growth and Transformation for Shared Prosperity and Improved Livelihoods, while engaging with regional commitments on environmental health.

a3285.speaker: 2018 Global Food Policy Report
a3285.name: 2018 Global Food Policy Report
a3285.speech: States that country-level leadership and champions who work to end hunger and malnutrition are among the most important drivers of change. Some encouraging campaigns include China’s commitment to achieving Healthy China 2030 and Ethiopia’s Seqota Declaration on ending under nutrition by 2030.

a3285.speaker: 2018 Global Food Policy Report
a3285.name: 2018 Global Food Policy Report
a3285.speech: Underlines that in the face of economic slowdown and a decline in export revenues, attracting Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) becomes critical to sustaining economic recovery. Findings show that FDI flows to Africa decreased by 3 percent in 2016 to USD 59 billion, with over half of total FDI directed to five countries: Angola, Egypt, Ethiopia, Ghana, and Nigeria; Egypt’s increase of 17 percent reflects the discovery of gas reserves, while the 28 percent decline in the Democratic Republic of the Congo followed the sharp fall of global metals prices. It also points out that in East Africa, FDI to Ethiopia increased by 46 percent, with rising investment in manufacturing and infrastructure, and in West Africa FDI grew by 12 percent, boosted by increased investment in oil and other natural resources in Nigeria and Ghana.

a3285.speaker: 2018 Global Food Policy Report
a3285.name: 2018 Global Food Policy Report
a3285.speech: Points out that continued poor rains in parts of Ethiopia, Kenya, and Somalia in late 2016 and early 2017 caused a major food security crisis, particularly in Somalia and Ethiopia. As of December 2017, emergency conditions were expected to continue in parts of the region into 2018.

a3285.speaker: 2018 Global Food Policy Report
a3285.name: 2018 Global Food Policy Report
a3285.speech: States that, although agricultural research spending and human resource capacity in Africa south of the Sahara have grown considerably, this growth has been uneven and trends are driven by large countries such as Ethiopia, Nigeria, and South Africa. “Many countries are overly dependent on volatile and unsustainable donor funds,” it reads.

a3306.speaker: Confederation of Mozambican Business Associations (CTA)
a3306.name: Confederation of Mozambican Business Associations (CTA)
a3306.speech: Insists that there is a shortage of foreign currency on the national market and this may lead to the bankruptcy of some companies ; has invited all companies with import invoices that have been unpaid for more than three months to submit copies of these documents to its offices so that they can be forwarded to the Bank of Mozambique for payment.

a3306.speaker: Bank of Mozambique
a3306.name: Bank of Mozambique
a3306.speech: Recently claimed that there is enough foreign currency to satisfy market demand.

a3306.speaker: Agostinho Vuma, CTA chairperson
a3306.name: Agostinho Vuma
a3306.title: CTA chairperson
a3306.speech: Speaking to reporters on Thursday in Maputo, said the lack of foreign currency on the national market may also contribute to an increase in inflation; presented documents pointing to the lack of liquidity in currency from commercial banks to customers, as well as a list of companies whose invoices were submitted to commercial banks for payment but not satisfied, explaining that the values of this list, submitted to the Bank of Mozambique, come to 402 million dollars over the third quarter of 2024 ; "The CTA hereby reacts to the central bank's position because it considers it to be insensitive to the problems that companies, as the drivers of the economy, have been facing. In the routine dialogue meetings with the Bank of Mozambique, the CTA took 15 representatives of the most affected companies to a working meeting with the financial system regulator to work on finding the reasons behind the problem. However, the regulator has never presented a straight answer" ; "From November 2023 to 2024 they fell by 12.8 percent. When the same analysis is carried out over two years, the reduction is more pronounced, at 47.5 percent. The sector most affected, excluding fuel, is manufacturing industry, particularly due to the import of raw materials and equipment" ; "Then follows the tourism sector, because international airlines have suspended ticketing in some agencies from Mozambique as a result of difficulties in repatriating the respective revenue, which must always be the dollar equivalent" ; believes that it doesn't make sense when the central bank insists that there are no foreign currency liquidity problems.

a3434.speaker: China's Foreign Ministry
a3434.name: China's Foreign Ministry
a3434.speech: Has confirmed Mr. Hichilema's visit, taking him to China from 10th to 16th September 2023.

a3575.speaker: “Seville Commitment” (UN-negotiated declaration text)
a3575.name: “Seville Commitment” (UN-negotiated declaration text)
a3575.speech: States that the objective is to “renew the framework of global development financing”, at a moment of “serious geopolitical tensions and conflicts” and when the goals agreed by the international community in the 2030 Agenda “are seriously behind schedule”. ; “We are running out of time to reach our goals and to confront the adverse impacts of climate change. (...) The gap between our sustainable development aspirations and the financing to achieve them has continued to widen, particularly in developing countries, reaching an estimated value of 4 trillion dollars a year.” ; Across 68 pages it also emphasises that only the strengthening of multilateralism, of international cooperation and of institutions such as the UN can respond to the urgent need to eradicate poverty and confront the impacts of climate change.

a3575.speaker: United Nations (UN calculations/figures)
a3575.name: United Nations (UN calculations/figures)
a3575.speech: According to the UN's calculations, the current shortfall in development aid is 1.5 trillion more than ten years ago, and in 2024 official development assistance fell for the first time in the last six years, with a further fall of 20% forecast for 2025.

a3575.speaker: Amina Mohamed, UN Deputy Secretary-General
a3575.name: Amina Mohamed
a3575.title: UN Deputy Secretary-General
a3575.speech: “It is regrettable that an important member state leaves the room in the face of issues so important for billions of people,” she said at a press conference presenting the Seville meeting last Wednesday. ; She added that the presence of more than 60 world leaders in Seville is a good sign and that she believes the US will end up being obliged to address, in one way or another, the commitments signed by the rest of the international community, so “that they can be part of the success of lifting millions of people out of poverty and achieving the sustainable development goals.”

a3575.speaker: António Guterres, UN Secretary-General
a3575.name: António Guterres
a3575.title: UN Secretary-General
a3575.speech: Said recently that the Seville conference “is a unique opportunity to reform the international financial system”, which today is obsolete and dysfunctional, adding: “In this turbulent context, we cannot let our ambitions evaporate.”

a3577.speaker: Shirley Ayorkor Botchwey, Ghana's Minister for Foreign Affairs and Regional Integration
a3577.name: Shirley Ayorkor Botchwey
a3577.title: Ghana's Minister for Foreign Affairs and Regional Integration
a3577.speech: Expressed grave concern about the deteriorating conditions of the Palestinian people due to the ongoing conflict in the Gaza strip. She reiterated the call for the cessation of hostilities, the removal of impediments to humanitarian assistance, and the release of all hostages.

a3577.speaker: Shirley Ayorkor Botchwey, Ghana's Minister for Foreign Affairs and Regional Integration
a3577.name: Shirley Ayorkor Botchwey
a3577.title: Ghana's Minister for Foreign Affairs and Regional Integration
a3577.speech: Underscored the need for a heightened commitment to multilateralism, urging Member States to prioritise the welfare of the most vulnerable. She also expressed concern about the growing prevalence of unilateral policies and actions across diverse areas including political, economic, and trade, and called for the repudiation of such trends. She further advocated for a return to cooperative frameworks to systematically address transnational challenges and cultivate international collaboration.

a3577.speaker: Shirley Ayorkor Botchwey, Ghana's Minister for Foreign Affairs and Regional Integration
a3577.name: Shirley Ayorkor Botchwey
a3577.title: Ghana's Minister for Foreign Affairs and Regional Integration
a3577.speech: Emphasised the critical need for reforming international financial structures to secure equitable and impartial access to finance for the global South. Commending the Africa Group at the United Nations for its efforts in advancing inclusive and effective tax cooperation, she urged Member States to unite in endorsing the appeals for reform within global institutions that may have deviated from their original commitments. She further stressed the need for worldwide support and solidarity to rejuvenate the economies of Member States and fulfill the aspirations of their populations for peace, prosperity, and dignity.

a3598.speaker: STV (independent television station) report
a3598.name: STV (independent television station) report
a3598.speech: According to a report on the independent television station STV, the sabotage of the road was spearheaded by drivers of the minibuses, known colloquially as “chapas”, which provide much of the passenger transport in Maputo.

a3598.speaker: Chapa (minibus) drivers protesting at the tollgate
a3598.name: Chapa (minibus) drivers protesting at the tollgate
a3598.speech: They warned the police that, if there was any attempt to disburse the protesters, they would blow up the [hijacked fuel] tanker.

a3775.speaker: Organizers of the handover ceremony
a3775.name: Organizers of the handover ceremony
a3775.speech: Said the outgoing minister was absent for "personal reasons."

a3775.speaker: Fatima Camara, new Guinean Minister of Commerce
a3775.name: Fatima Camara
a3775.title: new Guinean Minister of Commerce
a3775.speech: "I am the luckiest of ministers because I am going to continue the legacy of Dr Diaka Sidibe, a solid legacy that I pledge to respect and build upon," she declared before an audience of senior officials, members of the Government and representatives of the CNRD ; She praised the vision of President General Mamadi Doumbouya and of Prime Minister Amadou Oury Bah, while paying tribute to her family and her former colleagues at the Ministry of Fisheries: "I am leaving one family to join another" ; "This mission, I place under God's grace."

a3775.speaker: Fatima Camara, new Guinean Minister of Commerce
a3775.name: Fatima Camara
a3775.title: new Guinean Minister of Commerce
a3775.speech: Set out the broad lines of her roadmap, stressing the ministry's priority challenges: improving access to essential goods, modernising storage infrastructure, structuring domestic trade and strengthening Guinean exports, notably through digital commerce: "We will form an organised, rigorous team, focused on impact and committed to transparency. I am counting on each and every one of you to build a culture of performance."

a3775.speaker: Tamba Benoit Komano, Minister Secretary General of the Government
a3775.name: Tamba Benoit Komano
a3775.title: Minister Secretary General of the Government
a3775.speech: Delivered the official installation declaration on behalf of the President of the Republic and the Prime Minister: "In the name of the Head of State and the Head of Government, I hereby officially declare you installed in your functions. May God guide your steps."

a3883.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank
a3883.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank
a3883.speech: On December 13, 2023, confirmed Somalia hit the Heavily Indebted Poor Countries (HIPC) completion point, reducing external debt from 64 percent of GDP in 2018 to under 6 percent by end-2023 - signifying $4.5 billion in debt relief.

a3883.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a3883.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a3883.speech: Identifies "financial deepening" and strengthened central bank oversight as keys to unlocking private investment and domestic saving.

a3883.speaker: Oxfam
a3883.name: Oxfam
a3883.speech: According to Oxfam, every year, members of the Somali diaspora send approximately $1.3 billion to their friends and relatives in Somalia, exceeding all humanitarian and development assistance to the country and comprising between 25 and 40 percent of the country's economy.

a3883.speaker: Mohamed Sh Omar Ibrahim, CFO at Gargaara Finance Limited and former Economic and Financial Policy Advisor to the Office of the Prime Minister of Somalia
a3883.name: Mohamed Sh Omar Ibrahim
a3883.title: CFO at Gargaara Finance Limited and former Economic and Financial Policy Advisor to the Office of the Prime Minister of Somalia
a3883.speech: Argued that debt relief is "not the destination-it's a launchpad," and that Somalia's success "hinges on establishing a dynamic capital market and fueling private sector-led growth-a pivotal shift amid a constricting Official Development Assistance (ODA) landscape" ; warned that "global ODA is contracting. Major donors are pulling back, hampering financing in low-income and fragile states. This decline underscores that concessional capital is scarcer, scrutinized, and tied to outcomes. For Somalia, reliance solely on grants is no longer viable." ; urged that "Somalia must leverage private capital, tapping into diaspora savings, sovereign financing, diaspora bonds, and eventually international institutional capital... This is about more than growth, it's about self-reliance and determination. Somalia can't rely on outsiders alone. Its roads, schools, and jobs should be built with its own capital."

a3883.speaker: Gargaara Finance Limited (cited example)
a3883.name: Gargaara Finance Limited (cited example)
a3883.speech: Gargaara Finance Limited, a leading financial institution in Somalia, is facilitating access to finance for MSMEs and has disbursed over $30 million in loans, nearly half of it going to women-led businesses.

a3895.speaker: Donald Trump, US President (executive order)
a3895.name: Donald Trump
a3895.title: US President (executive order)
a3895.speech: Signed an executive order sanctioning the International Criminal Court, accusing it of illegitimate and baseless actions targeting America and its close ally Israel. The order said the ICC's recent actions “set a dangerous precedent” that endangered Americans by exposing them to “harassment, abuse and possible arrest” ; “This malign conduct in turn threatens to infringe upon the sovereignty of the United States and undermines the critical national security and foreign policy work of the United States government and our allies, including Israel.”

a3895.speaker: Israel
a3895.name: Israel
a3895.speech: Denies the alleged war crimes in Gaza for which the ICC issued an arrest warrant for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

a3895.speaker: Caspar Veldkamp, Dutch Foreign Minister
a3895.name: Caspar Veldkamp
a3895.title: Dutch Foreign Minister
a3895.speech: “The court's work is essential in the fight against impunity,” said on X.

a3895.speaker: White House memo
a3895.name: White House memo
a3895.speech: Accused the Hague-based ICC of creating a “shameful moral equivalency” between Hamas and Israel by issuing the warrants at the same time.

a3895.speaker: The White House
a3895.name: The White House
a3895.speech: Accused the ICC of placing constraints on Israel's right to self-defence, while ignoring Iran and anti-Israel groups.

a3985.speaker: Trinity Energy Group Board of Directors (press statement)
a3985.name: Trinity Energy Group Board of Directors (press statement)
a3985.speech: According to a press statement announcing the appointment, the company's Board of Directors has promoted Mr. Mugambi after serving for five years as deputy CEO, and has named Dhor Aher as Trinity Energy Ltd's Interim Country Manager for South Sudan.

a3985.speaker: Trinity Energy (letter to Eye Media CEO Stephen Omiri)
a3985.name: Trinity Energy (letter to Eye Media CEO Stephen Omiri)
a3985.speech: “We kindly request you to take note of these changes and any future correspondents related to Trinity Energy should be directed to the appointed individuals,” reads the letter, addressed to Eye Media's CEO Stephen Omiri.

a3985.speaker: Trinity Energy LinkedIn page
a3985.name: Trinity Energy LinkedIn page
a3985.speech: According to information on its LinkedIn page, the company owns millions of liters of fuel storage at its depot in Nesitu, which includes an additional 2 million liters of storage currently under development.

a4013.speaker: Moses Osime, Public Relations Manager of LG Electronics in Nigeria
a4013.name: Moses Osime
a4013.title: Public Relations Manager of LG Electronics in Nigeria
a4013.speech: Remarked: “What LG brings is the best of the Korean high-tech creations to improve the life of the Nigerian people. On this national celebration, we are stressing our vision as a flagship leader in this industry, showing our utmost goodwill to work and strengthen ties between our brand and the local communities, through presenting world-class technologies that transform lives in a positive way.”

a4013.speaker: Kim Pan-kyu, South Korean Ambassador to Nigeria
a4013.name: Kim Pan-kyu
a4013.title: South Korean Ambassador to Nigeria
a4013.speech: Said relations with Nigeria would be one of its most vibrant economic partnerships in the nearest future; said that with the Korean government’s commitment to increase its Official Development Assistance (ODA) funding to $10bn by 2030, as well as provide $14bn to Africa-based Korean companies by 2030, they would catalyse projects for cooperation with Africa, especially Nigeria ; “Since Nigeria is a leading economy and the biggest market in Africa, I believe that the partnership between Korea and Nigeria will be one of the most vibrant ones in the years to come.”

a4013.speaker: Kim Pan-kyu, South Korean Ambassador to Nigeria
a4013.name: Kim Pan-kyu
a4013.title: South Korean Ambassador to Nigeria
a4013.speech: Said he was excited with the level of acceptance of Korean culture, especially its music, by Nigerians, and that there was a huge potential for cooperation between the two countries in the creative economy: “When I first came to Abuja earlier this year, I was pleasantly surprised by Nigerian people’s high interest in Korean culture, such as Korean language, K-drama, K-pop and K-food. I had an opportunity to observe a K-food contest in Abuja and was deeply impressed by the Korean foods made by Nigerian chefs. When I observed the Taekwondo championship in Abuja recently, I had a feeling that in a few years, the number of gold medals that Korean athletes win at the Olympics may decrease due to brilliant Nigerian athletes.”

a4114.speaker: Health sector stakeholders in Tanzania
a4114.name: Health sector stakeholders in Tanzania
a4114.speech: Stakeholders say the move is a blow to developing nations and poor countries, including Tanzania, which depends heavily on WHO support in confronting health challenges ; Speaking to this newspaper, health stakeholders in the country said the US withdrawal from WHO is a blow to developing nations including Tanzania.

a4114.speaker: Dr Egina Makwabe, Chairman of the Association of Private Health Facilities in Tanzania (APHFTA)
a4114.name: Dr Egina Makwabe
a4114.title: Chairman of the Association of Private Health Facilities in Tanzania (APHFTA)
a4114.speech: said it is a major blow not only to Tanzania but to the whole world ; said the US contributes 30 percent of WHO’s budget, “if you look at the vaccines side, at Gavi (the international organisation that supplies vaccines), that programme of providing vaccines to poor countries — the US was the biggest contributor” ; said it has been providing large sums to deal with diseases such as tuberculosis, leprosy and HIV/AIDS and treatment for people living with HIV, all of which have been handled by that nation, contributing large sums, a large percentage ; “It is possible that it is withdrawing, but let us wait — it may yet give its contribution directly; but if it withdraws and halts assistance it will be a great tragedy. Because it helps with staffing systems, some HIV/AIDS and tuberculosis medicines, vaccines and the upkeep of various programmes.”

a4114.speaker: Dr Mugisha Nkoronko, President of the Medical Association of Tanzania (MAT)
a4114.name: Dr Mugisha Nkoronko
a4114.title: President of the Medical Association of Tanzania (MAT)
a4114.speech: said the US announcement has been received with shock around the world ; “This is a nation that is great economically; when it withdraws its WHO membership and orders that all contributions that were in the process of being disbursed be halted, it makes one think, and we cannot understand the reason that made the White House reach this decision” ; said that although President Trump gave several reasons, including the weak capacity WHO showed in handling Covid-19 in the US and that it saw the organisation as incapable of handling diseases, which made the US withdraw ; “The organisation is now at a crossroads in dealing with eight billion people whose health is now at risk if 30 percent of its revenue disappears. Personally I interpret this as an economic war between two great nations, the US and China” ; “The US is a founding country, it has made a great financial contribution to making the world a safer place; we have heard no complaint academically or technologically. We think democracy can be used to rescue this, but this is a ‘wake up call’ — all nations have a duty to put money into WHO, we must all be accountable for making the world a safe place to live.”

a4114.speaker: World Health Organisation (WHO) statement
a4114.name: World Health Organisation (WHO) statement
a4114.speech: WHO, founded in 1948 with the US among its founding countries and with 193 member states, says in its statement that over a period of seven years it has been carrying out reforms of its operations ; The statement, issued today, says WHO hopes the Trump government will reconsider and engage in talks that would continue the cooperation between the US and WHO in order to protect the health of millions of people worldwide.

a4114.speaker: President Donald Trump (executive order)
a4114.name: President Donald Trump (executive order)
a4114.speech: President Trump in his order said the US will stop providing money, assistance or US government resources to WHO ; Trump has also ordered the recall and reassignment of US government employees or contractors working in any capacity at WHO ; He said the US government will look for credible and transparent international partners to take over the essential activities previously carried out by WHO ; He also accused WHO of allowing Covid-19 to become uncontrollable and of ignoring the danger of the disease, which has caused the deaths of thousands of people worldwide ; President Trump blamed China for trying to cover up the outbreak and accused WHO of failing to hold China accountable ; He also accused the organisation of favouring China, part of those accusations stemming from its strong opposition to the US move barring travellers from China from entering the country, while he called the disease the “China virus.”

a4114.speaker: President Donald Trump
a4114.name: President Donald Trump
a4114.speech: Trump, in his first term as President, complained that WHO had failed to adopt urgently needed reforms and was unable to show independence from the inappropriate political influence of WHO member states ; “The WHO continues to demand unfairly onerous payments from the United States, far out of proportion with other countries’ assessed payments. China, with a population of 1.4 billion, has 300 percent of the population of the United States, yet contributes nearly 90 percent less to the WHO,” he said ; He said the US intends to withdraw from WHO, and that the letter of withdrawal to the UN Secretary-General signed on January 20, 2021 revoked the US request of July 6, 2020.

a4114.speaker: WHO statistics (data)
a4114.name: WHO statistics (data)
a4114.speech: According to WHO statistics, the US gave Sh3.25 trillion over the 2022 to 2023 period ; Other major contributors to WHO for 2022-2023 are Germany Sh2.16 trillion, the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation Sh2.10 trillion, Gavi Sh1.21 trillion, the European Commission Sh1.18 trillion, the United Kingdom and Northern Ireland Sh1 trillion; others are Canada Sh516.46 billion, Rotary International Sh448.1 billion, Japan Sh422.79 billion and France Sh407.6 billion.

a4674.speaker: Elections Coordinating Committee (ECC)
a4674.name: Elections Coordinating Committee (ECC)
a4674.speech: Has called on the Government of Liberia and relevant stakeholders to strengthen the legal framework of elections and fulfill campaign promises made to the Liberian people; has suggested that electoral reforms must be considered a top priority to strengthen Liberia's democratic gains over the past year.

a4674.speaker: Malcolm Joseph, ECC Chairperson
a4674.name: Malcolm Joseph
a4674.title: ECC Chairperson
a4674.speech: Spoke at a press conference over the weekend, urging the Legislature, National Elections Commission (NEC), and other stakeholders to reform the existing electoral laws; stated that the reform is integral to Liberia's democratic development; said Liberia has a foundational legal framework for conducting elections, but weak enforcement has stalled the implementation and enforcement of those laws; urged President Joseph Nyuma Boakai's administration to address the wider governance and development issues and concerns and respond to its campaign promises; proposed constructive engagement with electoral stakeholders, particularly institutions linked to electoral reform, naming the Legislature, the Ministry of Justice, and members of the Executive branch; suggested that electoral reforms must be considered a top priority.

a4674.speaker: Malcolm Joseph, ECC Chairperson
a4674.name: Malcolm Joseph
a4674.title: ECC Chairperson
a4674.speech: Said the ECC has already started meeting with members of the Legislature, international and domestic stakeholders, and political parties that support electoral reforms, describing this as a critical intervention to improve elections' quality and conduct.

a4674.speaker: Elections Coordinating Committee (ECC) (proposals)
a4674.name: Elections Coordinating Committee (ECC) (proposals)
a4674.speech: Has proposed that the government set a threshold for boundary delimitation and amend campaign finance laws and regulations; in the absence of constitutional reform, proposed that the government amend the New Election Law (NEL) to establish an ad hoc electoral tribunal and amend Section 6.8 of the NEL to increase access to electoral justice; proposed that the government amend the NEL so that the appointment of members of the NEC Board of Commissioners is subject to a public vetting process; proposed amending Section 3.1 (2) of the NEL to modify the eligibility requirements; suggested that the transition to a passive voter registration system can be made through regulation and amendment of Section 4.1 (2) of the NEL to increase the maximum number of registered voters from 3,000 to 4,000.

a4674.speaker: Malcolm Joseph, ECC Chairperson
a4674.name: Malcolm Joseph
a4674.title: ECC Chairperson
a4674.speech: Explained that the ECC implements the Liberia Domestic Elections Observation Activity with funding from USAID; stated that the ECC is Liberia's largest domestic election observation network, established in 2010, with diverse competencies, experiences, and expertise in democracy, elections, and governance.

a4714.speaker: Adama Barrow, President of The Gambia
a4714.name: Adama Barrow
a4714.title: President of The Gambia
a4714.speech: Revealed that The Gambia unsuccessfully drilled five wells for oil and gas exploration, and further revealed that two of the wells were under his watch and that it cost The Gambia 100 million dollars, wasted, with political words claiming 'prospects' ; Revealed that the two wells under his watch were FAR and Petronas, but failed to state which companies President Jammeh used and how much it cost.

a4794.speaker: Environmentalists
a4794.name: Environmentalists
a4794.speech: Say the hardwood trees from which these beautiful carvings are crafted are in danger of extinction.

a4794.speaker: A recent study on Zimbabwe's wood carving industry by local and international researchers
a4794.name: A recent study on Zimbabwe's wood carving industry by local and international researchers
a4794.speech: Discovered it has become a roaring business in Victoria Falls.

a4794.speaker: Moses Mugande, sculptor at the Elephant's Walk Shopping and Artist's Village curio market
a4794.name: Moses Mugande
a4794.title: sculptor at the Elephant's Walk Shopping and Artist's Village curio market
a4794.speech: "There is money in selling wood carvings" ; "We can even exchange some of our work for precious goods, or even formal wear suits" ; "No wood means no work for most ordinary residents in Victoria Falls."

a4794.speaker: Ndumiso Muleya, sculptor
a4794.name: Ndumiso Muleya
a4794.title: sculptor
a4794.speech: Denies using illegally obtained wood, but says that some of his colleagues have been fined for the offence ; "I get hardwood from the Forestry Commission. They supply hardwood that has died naturally, but it's not enough to satisfy the demand, as not many trees die naturally in the wild" ; "Wet wood is easier to work on than dry wood and most sculptors are tempted to poach wet wood instead of being content with the small supply of dry wood from the Forestry Commission."

a4794.speaker: Ndumiso Muleya, sculptor
a4794.name: Ndumiso Muleya
a4794.title: sculptor
a4794.speech: Although aware that the making of these large sculptures was depleting his country's hardwood trees, says it is the only way he and many other wood workers can support their families: "Starvation taught me the art of wood carving" ; "We entered this business because there are no jobs. Then frequent droughts brought more hardships, followed by economic challenges which brought more unemployment. Woodcarving is our only source of livelihood."

a4794.speaker: Environmentalists
a4794.name: Environmentalists
a4794.speech: Are calling on the Forestry Commission to introduce an environmental tag for the carvings to show the legality of the wood's source, arguing this seal of approval would help authorities to easily track and crack down on poachers; they have also asked the commission to spearhead a campaign to educate sculptors and their clients to trade only in wood marked with the environmental tags.

a4794.speaker: Victoria Falls Wildlife Trust, local non-governmental organisation
a4794.name: Victoria Falls Wildlife Trust
a4794.title: local non-governmental organisation
a4794.speech: "The market is there. Tourists will always buy, and now there is a high price paid for wooden sculptures. What would also help is if sculptors could use pine, which is exotic, but grows faster than hardwoods, which take years and years to grow" ; "But this trend is threatening our mahogany, teak and mukwa trees."

a4794.speaker: Moses Mugande, sculptor
a4794.name: Moses Mugande
a4794.title: sculptor
a4794.speech: "I have seen people selling these roots on the roadside. And, of course, when the roots are cut, the trees die."

a4794.speaker: Innocent Hodzonge, executive director at Environmental Africa (Zimbabwe-based non-governmental organisation)
a4794.name: Innocent Hodzonge
a4794.title: executive director at Environmental Africa (Zimbabwe-based non-governmental organisation)
a4794.speech: "The long-term damages this booming trade is bringing have yet to be documented, and when we see the damage it will be too late."

a5306.speaker: National Audit Office (NAO) of The Gambia (audit report on provision of farm inputs)
a5306.name: National Audit Office (NAO) of The Gambia (audit report on provision of farm inputs)
a5306.speech: Disclosed that farmers prefer the timely availability of fertilizer before they start planting, and reported that the delivery pattern of fertilizer in 2021 and 2022 was similar to that of 2020 when fertilizer was delivered to the Regions in June, July and August: "In 2023, there was a change in the delivery pattern of fertilizer when delivery took place in June in the NBR; in July in CRR/S, LRR, and CRR/N, and in June in URR and the WCR. There is still no adherence to the month of May target."

a5306.speaker: Farmers interviewed in the North Bank Region (NBR)
a5306.name: Farmers interviewed in the North Bank Region (NBR)
a5306.speech: Said fertilizer availability is usually late for most of them, and would prefer the product to be available before planting, so that they can apply it on time.

a5306.speaker: National Audit Office (NAO) of The Gambia
a5306.name: National Audit Office (NAO) of The Gambia
a5306.speech: Tasked the government to ensure that quality farm inputs such as fertilizer are made available to farmers in a timely manner, and explained that interviews with the Department of Agriculture, Regional Agricultural Directors, and groundnut farmers show that the ideal time for fertilizer to be available to farmers is the month of May, so that they can apply the product on their farms on time.

a5306.speaker: Ministry of Agriculture of The Gambia (response to audit finding)
a5306.name: Ministry of Agriculture of The Gambia (response to audit finding)
a5306.speech: Indicated that they have developed and validated a Fertilizer Policy with support from the Rice Value Chain Transformation project (RVCTP) and other stakeholders, that the Policy is awaiting parliamentary approval for its official endorsement and implementation, and that to ensure commitment in promoting the integrity of fertilizer procurement, a 10 percent performance bond as detailed in the contractual agreements of GGC will be implemented to address any default by suppliers of fertilizer as security.

a5306.speaker: National Audit Office (NAO) of The Gambia
a5306.name: National Audit Office (NAO) of The Gambia
a5306.speech: "The Fertilizer Policy explicitly mentioned the Ministry's commitment to ensure the importation of fertilizer at the right time. However, the policy remains silent on specifying the particular month of the year or the rainy season that should be designated as the 'required time' for fertilizer importation and distribution to farmers" ; noted that a specific timeframe for importing fertilizer is not provided in the policy, and that review of GGC's 2020 contract files found Fermagro delivered 5,500 metric tons of NPK 15:15:15 and 4,000 metric tons of NPK 6:20:10 with no documentation indicating actual delivery dates, so it cannot determine when the deliveries were made; the expected delivery date was July 21, 2020, but the lack of clarity indicates delay in fertilizer supply for 2020, while in 2021 Zeine Enterprise delivered 10,000 metric tons of NPK 15-15-15 earlier than expected ; "On the other hand, Gach Global's delivery was 5 days late according to the contract agreement, but the consignment arrived in May, the recommended time for fertilizer supply" ; in 2022 deliveries from both Zeine Enterprise and Gach Global were delayed, Zeine Enterprise taking 217 days to deliver 7,000 metric tons of NPK 15-15-15 and Gach Global 52 days to supply 5,500 metric tons of NPK 6-20-10.

a5306.speaker: National Audit Office (NAO) of The Gambia
a5306.name: National Audit Office (NAO) of The Gambia
a5306.speech: "Beside suppliers failing to deliver fertilizer on time, the GGC also failed to implement the 10 percent performance bond provided in the fertilizer contract files, which is contrary to what is stated in their response."

a5306.speaker: National Audit Office (NAO) of The Gambia
a5306.name: National Audit Office (NAO) of The Gambia
a5306.speech: Stated that after a recent restructuring initiative, significant steps such as the signing of contracts with an industrial company and the establishment of a comprehensive delivery calendar were made to advance the fertilizer program, and highlighted that the program also includes the finalization of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the GGC and the establishment of a designated account at the Central Bank of The Gambia (CBG) and with other affiliated financial services.

a5358.speaker: Dennis W. Hearne, U.S. Ambassador to Mozambique
a5358.name: Dennis W. Hearne
a5358.title: U.S. Ambassador to Mozambique
a5358.speech: “As world leaders gather in Glasgow at the 26th UN Climate Change Conference of the Parties (COP26), the U.S. Government is proud to announce the expansion of our more than 13-year partnership with the Gorongosa Project”; said the expansion includes “additional targeted, disaster-resilient programming so that Gorongosa communities are better able to recover from and thrive after cyclones and other climate-related stresses.”

a5396.speaker: Botswana Democratic Party (BDP)
a5396.name: Botswana Democratic Party (BDP)
a5396.speech: Has said that the allegations of the presence of an American army base in Botswana, repeatedly made by the leader of South Africa's Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF), Julius Malema, were partly fuelled by the Umbrella for Democratic Change (UDC) when in opposition, and holds that the UDC government should be in a good position to deal with the flak.

a5396.speaker: Kentse Rammidi, Secretary General of the BDP
a5396.name: Kentse Rammidi
a5396.title: Secretary General of the BDP
a5396.speech: "That theory has always been nonsense," said in an interview ; added that the UDC government is now grappling with the consequences of allegations it once used for political advantage ; "The government of the BDP always stated that the Thebephatshwa Air Base was solely financed by the Botswana Government and is 100% owned by Batswana. The UDC used to fuel the allegations. They are now in a good position to explain why they did so. This teaches us that we must never pervert national interests for politicking."

a5396.speaker: Julius Malema, leader of South Africa's Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF)
a5396.name: Julius Malema
a5396.title: leader of South Africa's Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF)
a5396.speech: Speaking at the 12th anniversary of the EFF party in Cape Town, called for the closure of the alleged American base in order for Botswana to conform to the reputation of the UDC as a progressive movement: "We say to our brother Duma Boko in Botswana that we will heed his call for the unity behind the rallying cry for our land and minerals to return." ; "We call upon him to also remove the American base in Botswana. We have no land that can be shared with America, especially in Southern Africa." ; "We have a new government in Botswana, and that government is progressive. Let us remove the army base of America in Botswana."

a5396.speaker: Gardee Godrich, deputy president of the EFF
a5396.name: Gardee Godrich
a5396.title: deputy president of the EFF
a5396.speech: Addressing the congress of the Botswana National Front in Palapye during the President's Day long weekend (20 July), urged President Duma Boko to close the US army base because "it would take seconds for the US to bomb Union Buildings" if the EFF assumes state power.

a5727.speaker: Central Bank of Nigeria (statement signed by Acting Director of Corporate Communications Hakama Ali)
a5727.name: Central Bank of Nigeria (statement signed by Acting Director of Corporate Communications Hakama Ali)
a5727.speech: Said Nigeria recorded a balance of payments surplus of $6.83 billion in 2024, ending three years of deficits; said that in 2023 the country posted a deficit of $3.34 billion and $3.32 billion the previous year, and that the 2024 surplus reflected the results of key economic reforms, better trade performance, and improved data quality.

a5727.speaker: Central Bank of Nigeria
a5727.name: Central Bank of Nigeria
a5727.speech: Also reported a significant improvement in data reporting, with net errors and omissions narrowing by 79.5 per cent to minus $5.10 billion, down from minus $24.90 billion in 2023, and linked the positive results to key reforms, including the liberalisation and unification of the foreign exchange market, stricter monetary policy to manage inflation and stabilise the naira, and better coordination between fiscal and monetary authorities.

a5727.speaker: CBN governor
a5727.name: CBN governor
a5727.speech: “The positive turnaround in our external finances is evidence of effective policy implementation and our unwavering commitment to macroeconomic stability.” ; “This surplus marks an important step forward for Nigeria’s economy, benefiting investors, businesses, and everyday Nigerians alike.”

a5825.speaker: Arthur Peter Mutharika, President of Malawi
a5825.name: Arthur Peter Mutharika
a5825.title: President of Malawi
a5825.speech: Announced a bold step during his inauguration at Kamuzu Stadium in Blantyre on 4 October 2025: Malawi will dispatch a high-level delegation to the United States to engage on critical national development issues ; acknowledged the challenges caused by suspended USAID-supported programmes during his speech, emphasizing that the delegation to the US would focus on reactivating suspended programs, attracting new investments, and securing technical support to enhance governance and economic resilience.

a5825.speaker: Arthur Peter Mutharika, President of Malawi
a5825.name: Arthur Peter Mutharika
a5825.title: President of Malawi
a5825.speech: Highlighted the broader implications of international cooperation, asserting that Malawi cannot achieve sustainable development in isolation ; "We must proactively engage with bilateral and multilateral partners to address pressing challenges like food insecurity, unemployment, and infrastructure deficits," he said.

a5825.speaker: Arthur Peter Mutharika, President of Malawi
a5825.name: Arthur Peter Mutharika
a5825.title: President of Malawi
a5825.speech: Expressed gratitude to the US and other partners for their historical support, underscoring that Malawi’s progress has always been intertwined with global cooperation; assured that the government would manage resources responsibly and ensure that assistance reaches those who need it most.

a5825.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a5825.name: Donald Trump
a5825.title: US President
a5825.speech: Sent a message of goodwill, to which the announcement came in response, signaling a continuation of a long-standing partnership.

a5825.speaker: Grace Phiri, mother of four in Mchinji
a5825.name: Grace Phiri
a5825.title: mother of four in Mchinji
a5825.speech: "When the clinics had no medicines, we felt helpless. We hope the government can restore these programs quickly," she says.

a5825.speaker: Dr. Ellen Banda, development economist based in Lilongwe
a5825.name: Dr. Ellen Banda
a5825.title: development economist based in Lilongwe
a5825.speech: Notes, "Malawi’s economic recovery depends not only on domestic reforms but also on international partnerships that provide expertise, financing, and credibility."

a5825.speaker: Peter Mbewe, farmer in Nkhotakota
a5825.name: Peter Mbewe
a5825.title: farmer in Nkhotakota
a5825.speech: "If these programs return, our farms can finally thrive again," he says.

a5957.speaker: Council of Ministers of Mali (communique), chaired by Army General Assimi Goita, President of the Transition
a5957.name: Council of Ministers of Mali (communique)
a5957.title: chaired by Army General Assimi Goita, President of the Transition
a5957.speech: Announced that at its ordinary session of Wednesday 16 April 2025 the Council adopted draft texts, made appointments and heard communications, including decrees approving the purchase of 21,543 tonnes of fertiliser from OCP-AFRICA for 9,838,580,000 CFA francs excluding VAT, the air transport contract for the 2025 Hajj with the Egyptair-Kalis Voyages-Sarl Group for 2,062,500,000 CFA francs, and the transfer to Les Mines de Lithium de Bougouni-S.A. of the large lithium mine exploitation permit awarded to Future Minerals-SARL at Foulaboula.

a5957.speaker: Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of Mali
a5957.name: Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of Mali
a5957.speech: Informed the Council of Ministers of the conclusions of the 4th edition of the Antalya Diplomacy Forum in Turkiye, in which he took part from 11 to 13 April 2025, saying the meeting allowed the dissemination of the major messages of the Transition in the fields of Defence and Security and on geopolitical issues, and reporting bilateral talks with his counterparts from Turkiye, Sudan, Venezuela and with the UN High Representative for the Alliance of Civilizations.

a5957.speaker: Ministers of Foreign Affairs of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES), panel “The Sahel: the future of regional integration”
a5957.name: Ministers of Foreign Affairs of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES)
a5957.title: panel “The Sahel: the future of regional integration”
a5957.speech: Provided the elements necessary for an objective understanding of the situation in the Sahel and of the efforts undertaken by the Confederation in the fight against terrorism, and communicated on the conditions for accession to the AES Confederation, the establishment of the confederal levy and cooperation between the AES Confederation and ECOWAS.

a5957.speaker: Minister of Agriculture of Mali
a5957.name: Minister of Agriculture of Mali
a5957.speech: Informed the Council of Ministers of Mali’s participation in the High-Level Forum “Dakar+10” held from 7 to 9 April 2025 in Dakar, Senegal, whose objective was to take stock of the 2013 Dakar Declaration on Irrigation and propose new approaches for resilient and sustainable irrigation systems and food and nutritional sovereignty in the Sahel.

a5957.speaker: Participants of the “Dakar+10” High-Level Forum
a5957.name: Participants of the “Dakar+10” High-Level Forum
a5957.speech: Validated the new regional irrigation strategy for the Sahel and formulated recommendations to stakeholders, notably the alignment of technical and financial partners’ financing with the policy priorities of States, the reduction of food imports through the development of irrigation, and the scaling up of irrigation solutions developed under the Regional Support Project for the Sahel Irrigation Initiative.

a5957.speaker: Minister of Industry and Trade of Mali
a5957.name: Minister of Industry and Trade of Mali
a5957.speech: Informed the Council of Ministers of the holding of the 2nd meeting of ministers in charge of Industry and Trade of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES), held on 10 April 2025 in Ouagadougou under the chairmanship of the Prime Minister of Burkina Faso.

a5957.speaker: Ministers of Industry and Trade of the AES Confederation
a5957.name: Ministers of Industry and Trade of the AES Confederation
a5957.speech: Adopted several key documents to accelerate regional integration, notably the timetable for implementing the recommendations of the Bamako meeting; took note of the conclusions of the work of the Confederation’s private sector organisations; and committed to implementing priority actions, harmonising import, export and transit procedures for two-wheeled vehicles within the confederal space, strengthening public-private dialogue, and developing joint projects such as a confederal power plant and a railway linking member States’ capitals and certain transit countries.

a5957.speaker: Minister of Crafts, Culture, the Hotel Industry and Tourism of Mali
a5957.name: Minister of Crafts
a5957.title: Culture, the Hotel Industry and Tourism of Mali
a5957.speech: Informed the Council of Ministers of the concept of the “Maliden Kura Talent Incubators”, a four-month professionalisation process for 25 young people per cohort under the Culture Mali 2025 project, and of the organisation of the 9th edition of the International Balafon Triangle Festival under the theme “The Balafon, symbol of social transformation in a new sovereign space”.

a5957.speaker: Minister of Health and Social Development of Mali
a5957.name: Minister of Health and Social Development of Mali
a5957.speech: Informed the Council of Ministers of the country’s epidemiological situation, marked notably by an increase in the number of confirmed dengue cases compared with the past week.

a5957.speaker: Assimi Goita, President of the Transition, Head of State of Mali
a5957.name: Assimi Goita
a5957.title: President of the Transition, Head of State of Mali
a5957.speech: Called on the population to strictly respect prevention and disease control measures.

a6076.speaker: Donald Trump, President of the United States
a6076.name: Donald Trump
a6076.title: President of the United States
a6076.speech: “France, thank you very much Emmanuel. I imagined Emmanuel standing somewhere behind me” ; “Where is he?” ; “I can't believe it! You're taking a low-key approach” ; “Today, he is my friend, that's great, good job, thank you very much Emmanuel.”

a6076.speaker: Emmanuel Macron, President of France
a6076.name: Emmanuel Macron
a6076.title: President of France
a6076.speech: Said before leaving Sharm el-Sheikh that Monday was “a real advance and a decisive step. But we must also get ourselves ready for what comes next”, recalling the importance of access for “humanitarian aid” to Gaza as quickly as possible ; “Among the challenges of the coming days, there is also the fact that journalists must be able to return to Gaza and show the reality.”

a6200.speaker: US Secretary of State (statement)
a6200.name: US Secretary of State (statement)
a6200.speech: "This unacceptable behavior places 5.2 million people in the region in immediate need of humanitarian assistance at even greater risk," read part of his statement, terming the military blockade of humanitarian access in Tigray "unacceptable".

a6200.speaker: United States (statement)
a6200.name: United States (statement)
a6200.speech: Termed the actions reprehensible and called on both the Eritrean and Ethiopian governments to take immediate action that will make their forces step back; the statement also called on all parties to comply with obligations under international humanitarian law, especially those relevant to the protection of civilians.

a6200.speaker: US Secretary of State (statement)
a6200.name: US Secretary of State (statement)
a6200.speech: Confirmed that there were many credible reports of armed forces in Tigray committing acts of violence against civilians, including gender-based violence and other human rights abuses and atrocities; it also highlighted the conduct of the Eritrean Defense Forces and Amhara regional forces, noting that they have been particularly egregious.

a6200.speaker: US Secretary of State (statement)
a6200.name: US Secretary of State (statement)
a6200.speech: Noted that the continued presence of Eritrean forces in Tigray undermines Ethiopia’s stability and national unity, calling upon the Government of Eritrea to remove its forces from Tigray; the US questioned why both Eritrean and Ethiopian authorities have repeatedly promised such a withdrawal, but have not acted.

a6200.speaker: US Secretary of State (statement)
a6200.name: US Secretary of State (statement)
a6200.speech: Urged the Government of Ethiopia to withdraw Amhara regional forces from the Tigray region and ensure that effective control of western Tigray is returned to the Transitional Government of Tigray; the statement implored Prime Minister Abiy and President Isaias to hold all those responsible for atrocities accountable.

a6318.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a6318.name: Marco Rubio
a6318.title: US Secretary of State
a6318.speech: In an interview with SiriusXM Patriot on Monday, stated that certain humanitarian programmes, such as PEPFAR against HIV in Africa, would be maintained, while others, judged ineffective or remote from American interests, could be eliminated ; insisted on the need to review the allocation of public funds: "We are going to get rid of the ones that don't make sense, and we are going to keep or even expand the ones that do." ; "We are not walking away from foreign aid. We are walking away from foreign aid that is stupid, that wastes the American taxpayer's money."

a6318.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a6318.name: Marco Rubio
a6318.title: US Secretary of State
a6318.speech: Reaffirmed his support for the President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR): "I am a supporter of PEPFAR. I was a member of Congress. I am now Secretary of State.
