It is a programme we want to continue." ; stressed that the aim of the programme was to reduce its scale progressively: "If PEPFAR is working well, it should shrink over time, not grow, because fewer and fewer people are contracting HIV or transmitting it to their children."

a6318.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a6318.name: Marco Rubio
a6318.title: US Secretary of State
a6318.speech: Specified that certain forms of humanitarian aid would remain in place, in particular when they respond to security concerns: "Questions such as: is famine going to destabilise a country in a way that would be harmful to our national interests and open the door to radical jihadists or to others who would want to take advantage of it? We are going to continue to do that." ; denounced the excessive broadening of the concept of humanitarian aid, considering that certain expenditures should not fall to the American taxpayer: "That doesn't mean these are bad ideas. Someone should do it. It just shouldn't be the American taxpayer," while giving assurances that waivers had been put in place to guarantee the continuation of life-saving programmes.

a6318.speaker: Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC)
a6318.name: Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC)
a6318.speech: Has announced the suspension of some of its humanitarian operations because of the abrupt halt to American funding, jeopardising the aid provided to roughly 1.6 million people, notably in Burkina Faso and Sudan.

a6553.speaker: Halima Daud, Deputy Minister of Health of Malawi
a6553.name: Halima Daud
a6553.title: Deputy Minister of Health of Malawi
a6553.speech: Has called on people across the country to walk away from myths and misconceptions which prevent them from using mosquito nets ; She highlighted that malaria remains a huge burden in the country, calling for concerted efforts among various stakeholders to effectively deal away with the disease by the year 2030: "Malaria remains a huge health problem in Malawi with everyone at risk. In 2023, as a country, 6.4 million cases were recorded with a total of 1,670 deaths" ; She further disclosed that malaria contributed to 25% of all out-patient Department attendance, 10% of all admissions and 12% of the deaths among all causes of deaths, creating a huge workload for health workers and pressure on drugs at all health facilities.

a6553.speaker: Dr. Janell Routh, USAID/Presidential Initiative on Malaria resident advisor
a6553.name: Dr. Janell Routh
a6553.title: USAID/Presidential Initiative on Malaria resident advisor
a6553.speech: Reiterated the U.S. government's unwavering commitment towards the fight against malaria in the country: "Let me take this opportunity to reaffirm the U.S. government's commitment to the fight against Malaria in Malawi. Over the past two decades, the United States has been steadfast in the fight against Malaria. Through PIM, we have made significant investments to support Malawi's efforts to reduce the burden of Malaria" ; According to Routh, since 2006 the U.S. government has provided financial and technical assistance to the Ministry of Health's National Malaria Control Program—which includes almost $400 million to support malaria prevention and control activities.

a6553.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a6553.name: World Health Organization (WHO)
a6553.speech: Has expressed optimism that the country will completely eliminate malaria by 2030.

a6553.speaker: Dr Michael Kayange, speaking on behalf of the WHO country representative
a6553.name: Dr Michael Kayange
a6553.title: speaking on behalf of the WHO country representative
a6553.speech: Said the country is making significant strides in the fight against the disease: "Cases of Malaria and also deaths related to the disease are dropping down continuously every year in the country—which is a positive thing as we look towards eliminating the disease by 2030. However, there is a lot that we need to do as a country to achieve that target."

a6553.speaker: WHO report
a6553.name: WHO report
a6553.speech: According to the WHO report, over 250 million people suffer from malaria globally per annum.

a6749.speaker: South African government (Pretoria)
a6749.name: South African government (Pretoria)
a6749.speech: Responded on Saturday to the US President's signing of a decree freezing aid to the country, highlighting a misunderstanding of South Africa's plans to expropriate land and describing the Americans' actions as a "disinformation and propaganda campaign."

a6749.speaker: South African Minister of Foreign Affairs
a6749.name: South African Minister of Foreign Affairs
a6749.speech: Said the United States has provided no evidence; that the text of the law stipulating the end of American aid lacks factual accuracy and does not acknowledge the painful history of colonialism and apartheid in the country; and that the expropriation will affect only infertile and unused land, not farmland that produces harvests.

a6749.speaker: Vincent Magwenya, spokesperson for President Cyril Ramaphosa
a6749.name: Vincent Magwenya
a6749.title: spokesperson for President Cyril Ramaphosa
a6749.speech: Said the South African President was disappointed by Trump's contempt for diplomatic channels of communication, and said in a television interview that South Africa has always had views different from those of the United States on certain issues but that the two countries have never experienced such an escalation of diplomatic tensions, and that a simple conversation could dispel these misunderstandings.

a6749.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a6749.name: Donald Trump
a6749.title: US President
a6749.speech: Offered white South Africans (Afrikaners) refugee status in the United States, saying their rights have been violated by the land expropriation decree.

a6749.speaker: Solidarity Movement (Afrikaner trade union)
a6749.name: Solidarity Movement (Afrikaner trade union)
a6749.speech: Declared that its members would remain in South Africa despite the US government's relocation offer.

a6749.speaker: Spokesperson for the Solidarity Movement
a6749.name: Spokesperson for the Solidarity Movement
a6749.speech: Said that they remained firmly attached to their country and to all its people, and that they had not asked and would not ask for sanctions against South Africa nor for the American government to cut its funding.

a6792.speaker: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, President of Somalia
a6792.name: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud
a6792.title: President of Somalia
a6792.speech: Openly acknowledged his government's growing fatigue after two and a half years of relentless combat against Al-Shabaab, stating in an exclusive interview with The Washington Post, “It's difficult because we have a limited capability. After two years of continuous war, we have some level of fatigue. But we are reorganizing our forces now, and there is a new campaign going on as I speak to you.” ; conceded that while his government has significantly degraded the militant group, the promise of its complete eradication remains unfulfilled.

a6792.speaker: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, President of Somalia
a6792.name: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud
a6792.title: President of Somalia
a6792.speech: Urged the United States to expand its military presence in the country, calling on Washington to bolster its military footprint and emphasizing the need for enhanced training, advisory support, and special operations: “What we ask of President Trump is not to pull out the American advisers and consultants who are supporting the training of our special forces. Indeed, we are requesting that the United States increase the number so that we can eliminate al-Shabab while President Trump is in office.”

a6792.speaker: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, President of Somalia
a6792.name: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud
a6792.title: President of Somalia
a6792.speech: Underscored the global implications of Al-Shabaab's activities, highlighting the group's ties to Al-Qaeda, its international agenda, and its threat to critical shipping lanes, and pointed to the militant group's strategic alliance with Yemen's Houthi rebels, noting, “Al-Shabab and the Houthis have a very good relationship. They are exchanging weapons and training.”

a6792.speaker: Observers
a6792.name: Observers
a6792.speech: Mounting warnings that Al-Shabaab is not only regaining resilience but also strengthening its operational capacity.

a6792.speaker: Somali officials
a6792.name: Somali officials
a6792.speech: Warn that the potential withdrawal of U.S. troops could create a security vacuum, allowing Al-Shabaab to intensify its operations and reclaim territories lost during more than a decade of conflict with African Union peacekeepers and Somali national forces.

a6849.speaker: Dr Chérif Saloum Diatta, President of Harakati Senegal
a6849.name: Dr Chérif Saloum Diatta
a6849.title: President of Harakati Senegal
a6849.speech: Has called for bold and evidence-based policy reforms to propel Africa’s structural transformation and regional integration, delivering the keynote address at the 2nd Annual Harakati Conference in Accra; stressed the urgent need to reconsider existing economic policies, particularly in light of the recent withdrawal of Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger from ECOWAS: “This year’s conference is not merely a celebration of African integration”, adding, “It is a critical moment to confront our structural weaknesses and pursue far-reaching policy reforms that will enable accelerated development and deeper sub-regional cooperation.” ; emphasised the potential of such reforms to restore vital trade corridors, reinvigorate transit-based economies, and empower cross-border communities that have long been central to Africa’s traditional trade networks: “The region must adopt robust economic and social policy reforms. Only then can we guarantee that all communities share in the benefits of progress, without anyone being left behind.” ; further underscored the need to move away from dependence on raw commodities towards value-added sectors such as manufacturing and services, while also reducing reliance on foreign aid and reinforcing democracy and economic freedoms.

a6849.speaker: The Senegalese delegation, including El-Hamid, Alassane Diouf and Ndeye Sokhna Gueye
a6849.name: The Senegalese delegation
a6849.title: including El-Hamid, Alassane Diouf and Ndeye Sokhna Gueye
a6849.speech: Expressed gratitude to the conference organisers and reaffirmed their commitment to collaborating with partners across the continent to realise Harakati’s vision of integration.

a7261.speaker: Manuel Homem, Angolan Interior Minister
a7261.name: Manuel Homem
a7261.title: Angolan Interior Minister
a7261.speech: Has said at least 22 people, including a police officer, have been killed and 200 others injured in protests against a rise in the price of fuel that began on Monday.

a7261.speaker: Manuel Homem, Angolan Interior Minister
a7261.name: Manuel Homem
a7261.title: Angolan Interior Minister
a7261.speech: “In the past two days, we have witnessed actions that amount to acts of vandalism and endanger public security in the provinces of Luanda, Huambo, Benguela and Huíla. However, we want to inform citizens that the overall public security situation in the country remains stable,” the minister said, adding that many buildings had been looted or destroyed across the country, including supermarkets, shops and banks.

a7261.speaker: Angolan police
a7261.name: Angolan police
a7261.speech: Say more than 1,200 people have also been arrested in what began as a strike by taxi drivers against the price hike and then escalated into one of the most widespread and disruptive waves of protest the country has seen in recent years.

a7261.speaker: Doctors at public hospitals in Luanda (anonymous)
a7261.name: Doctors at public hospitals in Luanda (anonymous)
a7261.speech: Told the BBC emergency services had been overwhelmed over the last 24 hours. “We have received many protesters with serious injuries, including multiple traumas. Sadly, some have died. We fear the death toll may be higher than the official figures suggest,” one doctor said.

a7261.speaker: Angolan presidency (post on Facebook)
a7261.name: Angolan presidency (post on Facebook)
a7261.speech: “The acts carried out by the protesters, worsened by the presence of infiltrators with criminal intentions, show that the phenomenon has gone beyond a mere demand and now represents a threat to public order.”

a7261.speaker: João Lourenço, President of Angola
a7261.name: João Lourenço
a7261.title: President of Angola
a7261.speech: Had downplayed concerns over the decision to raise the price of diesel by more than 33%, and told CNN Portugal the protesters were using petrol prices as a pretext to undermine the government.

a7261.speaker: Angolan taxi unions
a7261.name: Angolan taxi unions
a7261.speech: Which called a three-day strike, have distanced themselves from the looting and destruction, stating they do not support such actions.

a7261.speaker: British passenger on the cancelled Frankfurt-Luanda flight (anonymous)
a7261.name: British passenger on the cancelled Frankfurt-Luanda flight (anonymous)
a7261.speech: Told the BBC they were told it was due to the “political situation” in Angola.

a7261.speaker: Lufthansa spokesperson
a7261.name: Lufthansa spokesperson
a7261.speech: Confirmed the cancellation, saying “safety and security for our passengers and crew has top priority.”

a7261.speaker: US embassy in Angola
a7261.name: US embassy in Angola
a7261.speech: Advised “US citizens to remain vigilant and limit non-essential movement within Luanda.”

a7261.speaker: Patriotic United Front (FPU), opposition coalition
a7261.name: Patriotic United Front (FPU)
a7261.title: opposition coalition
a7261.speech: Said it stood in solidarity with “all layers of society currently experiencing the effects of the severe economic and social crisis Angola is facing”, adding this “was a result of public policies disconnected from our country’s reality, poor governance, corruption and the government’s lack of human sensitivity” ; however, the FPU also said it “strongly condemned” the acts of destruction of public and private property carried out by protesters.

a7503.speaker: Ethiopian Red Cross Society (ERCS)
a7503.name: Ethiopian Red Cross Society (ERCS)
a7503.speech: demands 9 billion birr to assess humanitarian assistance in the 4 regions affected by conflict and violence ; According to ERCS assessment on the current conflict and violence on the ground, a total of 0.53 million people are in need of humanitarian assistance in Tigray, Amhara, SNNP and Benishangul-Gumuz regions, which requires 9 billion Ethiopian Birr to provide general and supplementary food, non-food items, water and sanitation services and other essentials.

a7503.speaker: National Disaster Risk Management Commission (NDRMC) report of September 2020
a7503.name: National Disaster Risk Management Commission (NDRMC) report of September 2020
a7503.speech: indicates that flood has also affected 1,095,358 people, out of which 313,179 people were displaced across the country.

a7503.speaker: IRC (Red Cross society leadership as cited)
a7503.name: IRC (Red Cross society leadership as cited)
a7503.speech: has called its partners and volunteers to raise a 233,090,712 dollar fund, targeted to support 2,534,297 people affected in the four regions.

a7503.speaker: IRC (Red Cross society leadership as cited)
a7503.name: IRC (Red Cross society leadership as cited)
a7503.speech: suggests enhancement of the culture of nonviolence through provision of peace education to increase peaceful coexistence among people, better coordination and collaboration among humanitarian actors, and strengthening ERCS's emergency preparedness and response capacity at all levels for a better living.
